NO CURRENT VALUE IS WRITTEN HERE: this KR is computed, not asserted — `bin/lib § same_action_linkage` re-runs it on every read from `linkage.jsonl` and `.perry/events.jsonl`, and `perry-state`/`perry-goals` publish that number with `current_provenance.state: measured`. The population is the `main`-track rows whose own `add` event carries a `kr` key, which is the mark row D's gate left on every row it governed; `phase/003-storage-code.md § Definition of Done` item 5, restated 2026-08-31, is why the rows opened before the gate are phase 004's and not this denominator. fields.summary: bin/perry-task is to be split into one file per subcommand group. The split is deliberately left unsized for now: the markdown reader, the row renderer and the cell escaping are all on their way out of that file, and re-measuring once they are gone is cheaper than splitting it twice. RE-EXAMINED 2026-09-10 AFTER DESIGN-016 SHIPPED, AND THE ANSWER IS THAT THE REFACTOR DID NOT TOUCH THIS ROW'S SUBJECT. DESIGN-016 changed how arguments are interpreted -- a SURFACE declaration per tool, one parser in bin/lib -- not where code lives. MEASURED: bin/perry-task was 8294 lines at the branch base 4ebc0693 and is 8497 now, so the file GREW by 203. THE CONDITION THIS ROW SET FOR ITSELF IS STILL UNMET: it said re-measure once the markdown reader, the row renderer and the cell escaping have left. TASK-263 is done, but the two spans its evidence names as obsolete document representation are still in place -- norm at bin/perry-task:1183 and heading_matches at :1430. THE BLOCKER IS NOW USER-922 AND NOT TASK-263, which is the substantive change. DESIGN-016 section 8 asks whether the tool boundary should be redrawn by OBJECT rather than by mechanism -- one tool per register holding both its lane verbs and its store verbs -- and section 4 records explicitly that Decision 3 asked only whether the tool NAMES stay and never ruled on the axis. Section 1.4's prefix table is the evidence: the same four registers are named twice, singular against plural, verb-left against verb-right, in two tools that differ by one letter. THAT MAKES THIS ROW AND THAT QUESTION TWO ANSWERS TO ONE PROBLEM, NOT A TASK PLUS A QUESTION. Splitting perry-task by subcommand group first would make the by-object redraw a second cut through the same file, which is precisely the cutting-it-twice this row was deferred to avoid.

The defect is disclosed at three layers and fixed at none. The real and unfixed half is that one `updated:` field carries two different facts, 'when the register changed' and 'when the KR numbers were asserted', written at one site and read as freshness at another. The consequence is that staleness is computable only register-wide, so a report of 'stale 0' is not evidence that any individual number is fresh. The cheapest wrong outcome here is a fourth disclosure.

TASK-184, two steps down this chain, moves the same contract page that aiMark's two live asks -- TASK-415 and TASK-416, filed 2026-09-10 from aiMark's own reading of perry-goals/list/3.0 -- also move. fields.summary: With ids minted, okr.objectives[].id stops being absent and is filled from the store, and the published contract moves to 2.2 with its Not here section rewritten. Done when a consumer can address an Objective by id out of the payload instead of matching its title text. DEPENDENCY ADDED 2026-09-10: also waits on TASK-415, and the reason is coordination rather than logic. Both rows move perry-goals/list by a minor on the SAME PAGE, schema/goals-list-contract.md. This row fills okr.objectives[].id, which is a value-meaning change under the 2.2 precedent -- no key moves and the same key returns something different. TASK-415 adds the rule that a measured current may not carry a null target, which is a semantics entry on the same page. Whichever lands second has to renumber its minor and rewrite its changelog row, and two rows editing one changelog concurrently is how a version ends up claimed twice. TASK-415 goes first because it is the smaller change -- data plus one documented rule, no code -- and because aiMark is blocked on it TODAY: its page renders nothing for the most rigorously measured KR in the register. NO LOGICAL DEPENDENCY EXISTS BETWEEN THEM: 415 is about key results, this row is about objectives, and neither reads the other's field. If the sequencing stops mattering -- 415 lands, or is dropped -- this edge should be cut rather than waited on.

fields.summary: Found by the TASK-226 V4 reviewer 2026-08-30, who ran seven misparse traps where the author had run five. Three are NOT inert. read_conformance strips with strip('`  '), so a row whose path cell is in BACKTICKS — or indented, or inside a fenced block — parses to the same plain key as an undecorated row. Measured on a copy: it flips a real file from 'undeclared' to 'conformant', and the next legitimate perry-conform declare rewrites the whole file from the parsed declarations, LAUNDERING the decorated row into a plain canonical row indistinguishable from one a person wrote on purpose. This is the file that gates every write under ADR-004's enforce gate. TASK-226's RESULT files this class as 'inert ... never affects a verdict' — true of asterisks, false of the class. It did NOT cause TASK-226's phantom row: that row's elimination rests on a render fixed-point check the reviewer reproduced independently (23/24 declarations, 0 unreadable, render(parse(f)) == f on both actual files), which is a complete detector for the whole class. So the elimination stands; the argument offered for it does not.
fields.title: a backticked path in .perry/conformance.md parses to a plain key, so a decorated row can declare a file conformant and the next legitimate declare launders it into a real one

fields.summary: Found by the TASK-157 V4 reviewer 2026-08-30 while confirming that row's own audit. TASK-157's new guard requires every non-empty linked: value to RESOLVE against perry-goals list --level overall — resolve rather than shape-match, because KR-O9.9 has the right shape — and refuses to pass on zero values, via checked >= 8. That threshold is satisfied by phases 001 and 003 between them, both already correct. So a phase 004 authored with every linked: empty passes the guard untouched. It is the same shape as the defect TASK-157 exists to fix, displaced into the future: TASK-157 caught eight KR-to-OKR edges silently replaced by prose, and this lets the next phase drop all of its edges silently instead. TASK-157's own round is deliberately NOT widening the guard — changing what it requires is a scope decision rather than a template fix — so it is filed here.

fields.summary: Found by the TASK-203 round 5 V4 reviewer 2026-08-30, ruled non-blocking for that row and filed here. Measured: 10 canonical records lost, 10 gained, rc 0, and perry-lint going from '16 row(s) drifted' to '0 row(s) drifted' as the records are destroyed. Also reproduced on asks.jsonl on the zh fixture. TASK-203's invariant does not catch it and is not supposed to: USER-906 chose a COUNT rule, and 32 to 32 is not fewer. The reviewer's reason for filing rather than blocking is the part worth keeping — closing it needs a per-record IDENTITY predicate, which is round 2's door and the fifth predicate the amendment explicitly forbids, and no tool path reaches it today because every tool-produced case is a shrink and is already refused.

fields.summary: Found by the TASK-230 V4 reviewer 2026-08-30 and ruled non-blocking for that row. The refusal demonstrably fires end-to-end at rc=1 with no file written, and unaccounted() — the function behind it — is unit-tested. fields.summary: Reported by TASK-241's author against its own change, 2026-08-30, and not filed by it because the PMO owns the board. bin/perry-conform:423 render rewrites the whole file from the parsed declarations. fields.summary: Found by the TASK-241 round 2 V4 reviewer, 2026-08-30, and ruled non-blocking for that row. fields.summary: ROUND 4 FIXES IN at f8bc100, five commits. THE FIVE ITEMS: (1) it reproduced all three green mutations plus both bullet rewrites ON THE UNFIXED TIP FIRST, confirming the pin was green in all five, then took BOTH halves — the claim narrowed (class renamed to say it checks the bullet's VOCABULARY against the token spelled in tests/run, docstring states the measured gap) and the pin widened to catch both export spellings, with the refuse token anchored to a non-comment line. The dead-refusal-under-'if false' case stays uncatchable by string search and is recorded as such rather than papered over. (2) IndexError replaced by two FAILs with sentences, verified with both banners reworded. (3) case-differing spellings now accepted, comparison is 'test -ef' on device+inode. (4) relative paths REFUSED with their own banner and reason — decided, not incidental; the 17-spelling sweep re-run shows four changed, all in the intended direction, nothing became accept-everything. (5) 24 and 18 removed, grep returns nothing. TWENTY mutations, four green, all reported. MC1 is the most useful: reverting -ef to round 2's string comparison kills exactly one test and it is the new one — round 3's blindness finding, one layer out. THREE OF ITS OWN FIXES WERE GREEN UNDER THEIR FIRST MUTATION and were tightened: the relative-refusal assertion matched the word 'relative' in an explanatory paragraph rather than in the banner, setUp's terminator, and the doc pin would have passed on three empty sets. fields.summary: Measured across TASK-239's round and its V4 review, 2026-08-30. There are exactly THREE gate() call sites in all of bin/, and at least three writers reach a files[]-shaped path without passing one: perry-knowledge promote writes a files[]-shaped path with no gate (found by the TASK-239 author); bin/perry-tasks render --write rewrites BOARD.md ITSELF on an undeclared project under enforce, rc=0 and no warning, md5 confirmed before and after (found by its reviewer); and the decide lane, which TASK-239 settled as exempt by design. TASK-239 ships an UNGATED_BY_DESIGN surface whose stated job is 'the count line makes you think the rest is covered — it is not', and it currently lists ONE lane out of at least three, which is the same shape as the surface it exists to correct.
fields.title: ADR-004's 'every writer gates on it' is false of at least three writers, and nothing sweeps for the rest

fields.summary: MECHANISM FOUND 2026-08-30 by the TASK-249 agent while retracting a number this trap had produced: tests/parallel:283 prints a red module's stderr TRUNCATED TO ITS LAST 25 LINES, and nothing is visibly elided. test_diagnose fails twice; the second failure's FAIL: header survives that window and the FIRST ONE'S DOES NOT, so the first arrives as a bare traceback with no prefix. That is why the output offers three numbers that all look like a failure count — grepping ^FAIL: gives 3, summing the per-module FAILED (failures=N) gives 4, and the summary line 'N module(s) red' gives 3 — and only the sum is right. It has now caught three agents in twelve hours, one of whom had DOCUMENTED the trap in its own result before walking into it, and one of whom used it to accuse a correct measurement of being wrong. The truncation is the root cause: the missing prefix is not a formatting choice, it is a line that fell off the top of a 25-line window.
fields.title: tests/run's output offers THREE numbers that all look like a failure count, and two of the three are wrong

fields.summary: The two paragraphs TASK-243 wrote as its section 7 and which its V4 reviewer said should be rows rather than prose. FIRST, the fourth ending TASK-243 considered and rejected: 'a register write must not honour rows it did not address'. It was rejected because intake is position-keyed so the blast radius is real, and the reviewer accepted that rejection — but rejecting an ending inside one row is not the same as deciding the question, and today an ordinary write still carries every board row forward including ones the command never looked at. SECOND, the literal property TASK-243's own spec named and could not deliver: 'the drift report must not decrease while canonical records are being destroyed'. Its close was ruled acceptable, on the reasoning that the literal wording would require lint to report a disagreement that no longer exists and that the defect filed was the SILENCE, which is closed. What is still missing is a durable 'somebody has seen this' surface with a clearing condition — a place where a destruction stays visible after the write that announced it has scrolled away.
fields.title: a register write honours board rows it was never asked about, and the durable 'somebody has seen this' surface does not exist

fields.summary: SHARPENED 2026-08-30 by the TASK-234 round-4 review: 'perry-tasks render --write' is not merely a writer that ignores the gate, it is a command Perry HANDS BACK TO READERS. bin/perry-migrate section _plan_task_store prints it in a refusal, from a function that has plan.project_root two lines above and does not pass it — so a reader who copies it runs 'render --write' against whatever project their cwd happens to be in, and it rewrites that project's BOARD.md. The review calls this worse harm than the rc=0 no-op that failed TASK-234 round 3, because that one changed nothing and this one changes a file. That makes this row a hazard, not a tidy-up. RE-SCOPED 2026-09-11, AND THE TWO HALVES HAVE SEPARATE FATES. HALF ONE IS DONE: perry-tasks honours --dry-run. Measured today -- delete the store, run write --from-board --dry-run, and the store is NOT recreated. It was fixed under TASK-361 and V4 round 8 pinned it: the dry-run sweep now covers 8 of 8 commands with a per-command control, and making risks-render drop the flag reddens a named test where it was green before. HALF TWO'S ORIGINAL SITE IS GONE AND ITS SHAPE IS NOT. The row named bin/perry-migrate section _plan_task_store, which printed 'render --write' in a refusal while holding plan.project_root two lines above and not passing it. perry-migrate was DELETED by USER-910. But rule 1 says enumerate the category rather than chase the instance, and the category is alive: MEASURED 2026-09-11 ACROSS bin/, 27 hand-back sites print a perry-* command with no --root beside it, and 17 OF THEM HAND BACK A WRITER. The worst are the ones this row was about -- bin/perry-lint:3672 'perry-tasks render --write', :3810 risks-render, :3955 intake-render, :4081 asks-render, and bin/perry_md_store.py:1610 '{tool} render --write' -- because perry-lint is the tool a reader runs when something is already wrong, and the command it hands back rewrites whatever project the reader's cwd resolves to. THE HARM IS THE ONE THE ORIGINAL REVIEW NAMED and it is unchanged by the deletion: a reader copies a command Perry printed and it acts on a project Perry never named. THE DELIVERABLE IS NOW THE CATEGORY: every hand-back that names a writer carries the root it was talking about, and a test holds the count.
fields.title: bin/perry-tasks accepts --dry-run and writes anyway

fields.summary: Filed 2026-08-30 by the PMO from the TASK-234 round-3 sweep. Agents cannot mint ids or write the board, so the finding needed a row from this side. Sibling of TASK-234; the wall standard it violates is bin/perry-conform:360.
fields.title: bin/perry-lint hands back 22 commands and every one of them drops the root

fields.summary: POPULATION CORRECTED 2026-08-30 by the TASK-234 round-5 reviewer, which re-derived the census with its own instrument: the row's headline was over FOURTEEN tools, not twelve. Over the other twelve it is 42 handed-back commands / 208 mentions, not 63 / 232 — the difference is exactly perry-conform and perry-migrate's own 21/24, which TASK-234 has now fixed. So THIS ROW'S POPULATION IS A THIRD SMALLER THAN FIRST FILED. The counts that actually matter reproduce exactly: 25 rootless and 19 raw, with both splits confirmed. Two further corrections: of the '3 genuine' raw interpolations outside these tools, TWO INTERPOLATE THE VERB, NOT AN ARGUMENT, so the genuine count is 1; and the backtick residual TASK-234 sized at two is EIGHT, of which only the message_for pair is pinned — two of the unpinned six are 'perry-tasks render --write' and 'write --from-board', the ones that WRITE. Whoever takes this row should re-derive the census a third time rather than inherit any of these numbers: it has now been measured three times and been wrong twice.
fields.title: Perry never shell-quotes a path into a command it hands a reader — shlex appears nowhere in bin/ or viewer/

fields.summary: Filed 2026-08-30 from the TASK-249 round-4 result. The agent found it in its own instrument, reported it rather than quietly re-running, rebuilt the copy and re-ran the mutations. That is the right handling, and it is also why the defect is worth a row: the harness pattern is prescribed by the PMO in every brief, so this is a defect in the project's verification discipline and not in one agent's script.
fields.title: The mutation harness's md5 restore-check is circular: it compares the file to bytes it just wrote

fields.summary: The ignored-path/name set is bounded configuration and belongs in a typed schema or manifest, not in a prose bullet that Python searches. Preserve the foreign-project safety behavior by validating the structured set directly.
fields.title: The ignored-name bullet pin asserts a substring, not a bullet, and one satisfying string blinds the guard to BOARD.md

fields.summary: Filed 2026-08-30. It surfaced the first time the module ran in the live repository. The PMO caused the write; the fragility is the test's.

fields.summary: Filed 2026-08-30 from the TASK-234 round-5 review. Item (b) is the interesting one: the row's defence is a choke point PLUS a source rule, and the source rule is the half that makes the choke point more than a convention — so its recall is the property the whole shape rests on. fields.summary: TASK-050 ran 11 rounds against a universal negative and PASSed on the round the criterion became decidable. Measured: 22 of 49 finding headlines audit the round's own artifact, not the product.
fields.title: V4 criteria must be bounded, and the round stops auditing its own exhibit

fields.summary: 23 records, all route: declare, all Perry's own files, zero migrations and zero disagreements. The gate's value needs a foreign project that drifts, and Perry has never been run on one. The delete list said 'delete bin/perry-conform, 974 lines'; that was wrong — 598 lines are the dead ledger and ~280 are helpers four tools depend on, so the file is gutted, not removed.

fields.summary: A render has to show which of the things it prints are canonical records and which are projections of them, or a reader cannot tell what is safe to edit. Blocked in practice on the two rows that create the render this property has to hold on. It replaces TASK-199, which carried the same scope and was dropped in error on 2026-09-01 in a way that could not be reversed.
fields.title: The render must distinguish what is projected from what is canonical — TASK-199's scope on the surface ADR-010 creates

fields.summary: Measure bin/perry-task and bin/perry-lint by call site against ADR-007's actual boundary: typed deterministic operations, opaque document transport/rendering, agent-owned prose interpretation, and obsolete document representation. The report is the detailed input to TASK-099 and must not classify by grep.
fields.title: Measure the category split inside perry-task and perry-lint by call site, not by grep

fields.summary: DESIGN-022 phase B, widening this row. Its original scope stands — a writer for KR records at both levels, overall in okr.jsonl and phase in linkage.jsonl, covering add, restate and withdraw — and gains perry-goals check <KR> (declares a typed check; refuses increase with target <= baseline, decrease with target >= baseline, done with a target other than 1, and a baseline on a limit) and perry-goals measure <KR> --check S --value N --evidence <path> (appends one measurement record and one measure event; refuses an undeclared check, a KR in COMPUTED_KR_METRICS, a missing evidence path, a scored phase or a non-current OKR version, and a bare overall id that names more than one version). Every refusal names the command that would make it pass. TASK-231 closes with this row.
fields.title: DESIGN-022 B — goals writes KR records, their checks and their measurements

fields.summary: Thin perry-state to the published payload over typed stores and deterministic filesystem facts. Preserve the payload shape, but remove reads that parse OKR, phase, design, ADR, role, knowledge or spec prose; expose opaque document references for agents instead.
fields.title: Thin perry-state to a query over the six JSONL stores; the payload shape does not change

fields.summary: ADR-012 decided that an agent should detect when a projection is behind the store it is derived from, and nothing in Perry surfaces that. This is the whole implementation of the detection half: a per-pair mtime comparison replacing about 3,100 lines of drift census. Perry's own history is the argument for building the surface rather than writing the instruction — an instruction with nothing behind it does not get run.
fields.title: Nothing tells an agent a projection is behind its store — ADR-012's rule has no surface

fields.summary: Perry reports six stores and names five of them. The tasks store alone prints `store: 225 record(s)` and `drift against the store`, where the other five say risks store, OKR store, config store, intake store and ask store — so the one line a reader is most likely to be looking at is the one that does not say what it is about.
fields.title: the tasks store is the only one of six whose census line does not name it: 'store: 225 record(s)' and 'drift against the store', where the other five say risks/OKR/config/intake/ask store

fields.summary: The top-risks reader still builds its answer from `BOARD.md` even though `perry/risks.jsonl` exists and is canonical. The task and OKR readers sitting next to it in the same file already prefer their stores, so this one reader is the odd one out rather than the norm.
fields.title: viewer/parsers.py:3899-3900 builds top_risks from BOARD.md while perry/risks.jsonl exists, reached from perry-state:1631 — the task and OKR readers beside it already prefer their stores (TASK-095 V4 round 1, finding 4)

fields.summary: A test module passes when run alone and fails three identity assertions when run under `unittest discover`, because of a module double-import artifact. Two reviewers observed it independently on 2026-08-29. The defect worth fixing is not the assertions: it is that the suite's answer depends on which runner invoked it and nothing anywhere says so.
fields.title: test_risks_store's TestTheReadersAreOneFunction fails 3 assertIs identity checks under 'unittest discover' and passes under 'bash tests/run' and in isolation — a module-double-import artifact, independently observed by two reviewers on 2026-08-29; the suite's answer depends on the runner and nothing says so

fields.summary: Re-measured 2026-09-16 before dispatch (evidence/2026-09/TASK-270-reproduction-2026-09-16.md). The original trigger, perry-config write --from-file, was removed by DESIGN-016, and 'refused forever' no longer holds: perry-config set recovers. What remains is reproduced: unsetting every setting leaves .perry/config.jsonl with zero records, exit 0 throughout; perry-task add then refuses saying the store 'holds records that do not validate' and tells the user to find them with perry-lint; perry-lint says '0 record(s), all valid' and also reports the Perry-written file as NS-01 foreign state. None of the three messages names the recovery. The writer and the linter disagree about whether an empty store is usable, and two of the messages are false.

fields.summary: `tracks_source` appears on two published payloads with four possible values and has no entry in the schema or in any reference page — so a consumer reading it has to guess what the values mean. Two consecutive reviewers raised it before it was filed.
fields.title: tracks_source is on two published payloads (perry-state project.config, perry-diagnose work_modes) with four possible values and no entry in schema/ or reference/ — raised by two consecutive TASK-095 reviewers

fields.summary: A host-support test is flaky under the parallel runner: red once on 2026-08-29 with an empty in-flight cache, green in isolation and green on two consecutive re-runs. Same class as the queue-reconcile and scratchpad-baseline races already on the board — a concurrency defect that only appears under load.
fields.title: test_host_support.TestOpenCodeDispatchLimit.test_concurrent_mixed_registers_do_not_exceed_global_cap is FLAKY under the parallel runner — red once on 2026-08-29 with an empty ~/.cache/perry/in-flight, green in isolation and green on two consecutive tests/run re-runs; same class as the already-filed queue-reconcile and scratchpad-baseline parallel races

fields.summary: Duplicate ids destroy records silently, in two different directions. A duplicate on the BOARD deletes a stored risks or asks record on an ordinary write, because the record builders skip an id they have already seen; a duplicate IN THE STORE leaks one record's cleared state onto the other and then persists it. Both predate TASK-203 and neither was reachable before it.
fields.title: duplicate ids: a duplicate on the BOARD silently deletes a stored risks/asks record on an ordinary write (risk_records/ask_records skip a seen id), and a duplicate IN THE STORE leaks one record's cleared onto the other and re-persists it — both predate TASK-203 and were unreachable before it

fields.summary: Re-ordering the tracks table in `.perry/config.md` by hand reads as config-store drift to perry-lint and as nothing at all to every other tool. The behaviour is defensible under the principle as written, but it is neither documented nor guarded. The reviewer who found it also notes that two neighbouring behaviours were each verified against only one fixture.
fields.title: a hand-REORDERED .perry/config.md § Tracks table is config-store-drift to perry-lint and silent to every other tool — defensible under principle A as written, but neither documented nor guarded; found by the TASK-095 round 6 V4 reviewer, who also notes records_out_of_stored_order and cells_wearing_decoration were each verified against only one fixture

fields.summary: After an intake sweep empties the canonical intake store, perry-lint reports `perry/intake.jsonl` as foreign state Perry did not write — even though the intake contract says an empty file is still a store. The fix has to recognise Perry's own declared empty store without also excusing a foreign file that happens to share the name.
fields.title: after intake-sweep leaves the canonical intake store empty, perry-lint reports perry/intake.jsonl as NS-01 foreign state even though the intake contract says an empty file is still a store; recognize Perry's declared empty intake store without excusing a foreign same-name JSONL

fields.summary: The first row of DESIGN-015's implementation plan, locked 2026-09-02: declare `linkage.jsonl` in Perry's claims list and write the three record schemas it will hold. Section 7 of that design carries the risk this creates — a new claimed path means a new namespace-collision warning in every existing Perry project.
fields.title: DESIGN-015 A — declare linkage.jsonl in claims[] and write its three record schemas

fields.summary: The second row of DESIGN-015: import the linkage records that currently live in `phase/003-linkage.md` into the new store. The count filed with the row is a measurement rather than an estimate, so it is to be re-measured before importing and the difference reported if the register has moved.
fields.title: DESIGN-015 B — import the 93 linkage records from phase/003-linkage.md into the store

fields.summary: The third row of DESIGN-015, and the one the whole sequence turns on: move the six linkage readers onto the store. It MUST land before the add-time writer, and the ordering is a hard constraint rather than a preference — a writer pointing at a store the readers have not moved to fails silently, with the edge landing while every reader still answers from the old document.
fields.title: DESIGN-015 C — move the six linkage readers to the store

fields.summary: The fourth row of DESIGN-015: `perry-task add --kr` writes the linkage edge itself and the add event carries it, which is what moves phase KR P003-O3-KR2 off zero. Blocked on the reader migration by the hard ordering constraint that row records. The design flags its own reading of user decision 3 as an interpretation, so if an explicit never-asked record was intended, this row changes with it.
fields.title: DESIGN-015 D — add --kr writes the edge, and the add event carries kr

fields.summary: The fifth row of DESIGN-015: `phase/<NNN>-linkage.md` sheds the half of itself that is schema'd data once that data lives in the store. Separable and allowed to lag — unlike the add-time writer it does not gate P003-O3-KR2 — and it is DESIGN-013 hygiene rather than work serving that KR.
fields.title: DESIGN-015 E — phase/<NNN>-linkage.md sheds its schema'd half

fields.summary: The sixth row of DESIGN-015. It is what turns phase KR P003-O3-KR2 from a number somebody typed into a number something counted, by computing it from the linkage store and the event log. It should not be allowed to lag the rest of the sequence for that reason.
fields.title: DESIGN-015 F — P003-O3-KR2 is computed from the store and events, not asserted

fields.summary: The task-to-design half: an implementation row need not cite the design it implements, so a finished design can report as never handed off forever. The trap was measured as it fired — filing this row took DESIGN-001 from `impl_refs` 0 to 1 and emptied the pending list, with nothing implemented, because the counter is a literal text match. So the defect is two-sided: six real implementation rows count for nothing, and one row that merely says 'read DESIGN-001' counts as implementing it.
fields.title: a locked design's implementation rows need not cite it, so a finished design reports as never handed off forever

fields.summary: perry-lint reads the track register out of `.perry/config.md` after resolving the project root, so on a project that keeps its config only in the store it returns no tracks rather than that project's own. It is strictly better than reading a FOREIGN register and it is still not reading `.perry/config.jsonl`. Reported by another row's agent rather than folded into that round, which is why it is a row instead of scope creep.
fields.title: perry-lint's _track_context reads the track register from .perry/config.md after the walk, so a store-only project gets no tracks rather than its own
35% of specs pass the dispatch safety gate because it cannot see their scope at all, and the documented add-task procedure is what produces them

fields.summary: dispatch.md tells a dispatched agent to branch but never to isolate, so a subagent switches the SHARED working tree and the PMO's own writes land on that agent's branch. Blocked awaiting a user decision after the round exhausted its review budget with two failures.
fields.title: dispatch.md tells an agent to branch but never to isolate, so a subagent switches the SHARED working tree and the PMO's writes land on its branch

fields.next_action: Make the spec-authoring path ask for the ## Bound that review.md §1 already requires; use TASK-247's missing Bound and the 2026-09-02 review census as evidence. Keep bounded acceptance explicit before review, where omission currently costs rounds. See perry/evidence/2026-09/TASK-447-next-action-accounts.md#task-286.
fields.summary: review.md requires a bounded criterion and perry-lint reports its absence, but add-task — the only place a spec is ever written — never mentions `## Bound`. So specs are authored without one and the omission surfaces rounds later, which is a measured cost rather than a style preference: one row burned five review rounds, another eleven, and a census found the unbounded finding eight times across twelve review files.
fields.title: the Bound that review.md requires is never asked for where specs are written, so its absence costs rounds instead of minutes

fields.summary: Nothing warns an author against writing a cross-reference to a task id that has not been minted yet, and the id guessed may land on the row doing the guessing. Observed when a row's next action said 'unlike TASK-280' predicting what the NEXT row would be numbered, and that row was itself minted as TASK-280, making the sentence self-referential. The existing rule forbids an example id that resolves to nothing; this one resolves, to the wrong row.
fields.title: nothing warns against writing a cross-reference to a row that has not been minted yet, and the id it guesses may land on the row doing the guessing

fields.summary: The git-boundaries page never says how to write a commit message, and Perry's documentation convention is backticked identifiers — so a `-m` string containing them has them executed by the shell and substituted away. It happened: a commit explaining the escalation gate's false positives named two fragments and shipped with both names simply gone. This bites Perry harder than most projects because nearly every honest commit message about its own code contains backticks.
fields.title: git-boundaries.md never says how to write a commit message, and Perry's own identifiers are backticked, so a -m string silently executes them

fields.summary: perry-task's `--actor` is optional and defaults, so a write to a lane-owned file can end up with no owner any session can claim. The actionable core is that optional actor, NOT the incident that exposed it — five link edges were written that the session filing this could not account for, and the edges themselves turned out to be correct. The tool's own help already states the open question: DESIGN-004 asks whether actor should be mandatory and until that is answered an unset actor is recorded as unset.
fields.title: perry-task's --actor is optional and defaults, so a write to a lane-owned file can have no owner any session can claim

fields.summary: The dispatch safety gate matches a path a spec merely CITES as though the spec were going to write it. Both directions are live and one is silent: honest specs are refused for naming the evidence file the round exists to produce, and one spec passed only because an incidental mention elsewhere cancelled a real hit, with no output distinguishing that from a genuinely clean scan. Same defect family as a design-id counter that cannot tell 'implements' from 'mentions' — a literal matcher standing in for intent.
fields.title: the dispatch gate matches a path a spec CITES as if the spec wrote it, so an honest spec is refused and an incidental mention green-lights a real hit

fields.summary: A V4 close still must fail closed without a valid fresh-review record, but the verdict must be a typed review artifact/store entry rather than a block parsed from review Markdown. Evidence prose remains an agent-authored document linked by id.
fields.title: close-task warns after the fact on a V4 whose verdict block cannot be parsed, so 10 of 27 V4 closures carry a rung nothing confirms
impl_refs walks up four directories for an event log, so a fixture test reads the host repository's state and a PMO prose edit reddens the suite
the design register has no reverse index: eleven corrections were written into the new document and never back into the old one

fields.summary: Every namespace-collision warning Perry emits is about a file Perry itself wrote, and the remedy each one offers is a no-op — the warnings say 'move Perry's state to its own root' and the state root already IS that root. One of the five is a separate bug: a FILE claim whose warning tells the reader to move files out of a file. This is why every lint run reported warnings that every session skipped as pre-existing; a check that only ever cries wolf gets trained out of the reader.
fields.title: every NS-01 warning Perry emits is about a file Perry itself wrote, and the remedy each one offers is a no-op

fields.summary: A scanner's heading-depth test does not cover the claim its own docstring makes. Reported by a reviewer as a green mutation and correctly not charged as a failure — a green mutation is a finding either way, and here it is the second half of one: the guard does not test what it says it tests.
fields.title: the objective scanner's heading-depth test does not cover the claim its own docstring makes

fields.summary: A typed title is verified by transport completeness, not by judging whether its prose is good. Every stored title must reach the published payload/render verbatim, and verify must fail when a renderer silently ignores the field.
fields.title: a store record's title field is unverifiable: planted garbage passes verify with drift 0 and byte_identical true

fields.summary: A parser's docstring says the walk is skipped when it is handed an exact root, and the code walks four levels anyway. CLOSING IT COSTS MORE THAN THE DOCSTRING GAP SUGGESTS and a correct fix will look like a regression unless it lands with its tripwire: the minimal fix turns another round's deliberate anti-vacuity test red, so whoever takes this must retire or invert that test in the same commit. Whether the minimal form is green suite-wide is unverified and should be established first.
fields.title: parsers.py:462 says the walk is skipped when handed an exact root, and the code walks four levels anyway

fields.summary: A dispatched agent's process cleanup matches across the whole machine and killed another agent's test suite. This is what concurrency looks like when the isolation is per-worktree but the process table is shared: the dispatch limit reserves slots and nothing scopes a signal. Worth pairing with the finding that the shared scratchpad is not private either — both are the same shape.
fields.title: a dispatched agent's pkill matches across the whole machine and killed another agent's suite

fields.summary: A line count in an evidence document was produced by an instrument that walks the filesystem rather than the git index, so untracked bytecode was counted into it. The lesson this row should carry is about instruments and about propagation: the wrong REASON for the wrong number had already been written into a locked design document, and correcting the board cell did not correct the artifact. A reviewer found it there and failed the round, correctly. A finding already written down somewhere needs the write chased, not just the record amended.
fields.title: an evidence document produced a line count with an instrument that walks the filesystem, so it counted untracked bytecode

fields.summary: DESIGN-014's per-tool line counts drifted and were not re-measured when the document was locked. Small on its own, but that document's whole method IS per-tool measurement, so a stale figure in it is the document failing its own standard rather than a typo.
fields.title: DESIGN-014's per-tool line counts drifted and were not re-measured at lock

fields.summary: schema/README.md tells a consumer to read the state root out of `.perry/config.md`, which is the projection rather than the register. Measured 2026-09-02, and the measurement makes the fix sharper than 'the page is stale': the tool resolves the state root itself and publishes it, including on a project that has no store, so a consumer that can run the tool never needs to parse the markdown and one that reads the store alone would get it wrong.
fields.title: schema/README.md still tells a consumer to read the State root out of .perry/config.md, which is the render

fields.summary: bin/perry-config's help text names a tool that was deleted. The argument that decides it came from the consumer who reported it: the guidance says to believe the contract table over the help text, but the help text is what a person actually runs — so Perry told a consumer to prefer one surface over another instead of fixing the one people invoke.
fields.title: bin/perry-config --help names perry-conform, a tool TASK-261 deleted
33 test modules walk the whole tree and none excludes .claude/worktrees, so every one scans ten times the repository
tests/durations.json schedules a module that no longer exists at the head, and records the real binding module 10x low

fields.summary: A design document's entry cites the branch it measured by a moving ref, so its figure stops re-deriving the moment that branch advances. Recorded by two consecutive reviewers and deliberately not charged by either, because it sits outside the round's bound and the review rules forbid widening one except by filing a row. This is that row. The item had already degraded further between the two rounds, which is the argument for it rather than against it.
fields.title: DESIGN-014's D-02 entry cites the branch by a moving ref, so its figure stops re-deriving the moment the branch advances

fields.summary: One half of a spec-scanning function de-duplicates across sections and the other half does not. Deferred in 2026-08 with a stated condition — the next change to that function — and the condition has now fired, so the deferral discharges into a row rather than expiring silently, which is the whole point of attaching a condition to one. Still cosmetic today: no spec repeats a fragment across two sections.

fields.summary: Three more test fixtures carry a `.perry/` directory with no event log, so the same parent walk escapes them too. Inert today for exactly one reason — none of the three ships a design directory — and adding a single design document to any of them re-opens the defect there with no warning and no test. Sequence it after the walk fix: if that makes the walk honour an explicit root, these three may need nothing at all.
fields.title: three more fixtures carry a .perry/ with no events.jsonl, so the four-parent walk leaves them too

fields.summary: Almost every spec on this project — 127 of 134 — carries no `## Bound`, and the check that would report that cannot fire until after the round it would have bounded. The check is implemented and correct and it reports two, because it reads the criteria field OF A VERDICT BLOCK — so a spec is only reachable once a review has already been written against it. A post-hoc check on a pre-flight property. The two it does fire on belong to the row that failed two review rounds and hit the schema limit: it found the unboundedness by paying for it twice.
fields.title: 127 of 134 specs carry no ## Bound, and the check that would say so can only fire after the round it would have bounded

fields.next_action: Design dispatch checkpointing so the first commit precedes any expensive work, including baseline tests. TASK-155 lost its round at the 600s watchdog with zero commits; 'commit evidence before a long run' failed because the baseline itself was the first long run. See perry/evidence/2026-09/TASK-447-next-action-accounts.md#task-309.
fields.summary: Nothing a dispatched agent does reaches disk until its single terminal commit, so an interruption at any point before that costs the whole round. Measured on 2026-09-02: five agents were dispatched, the laptop was closed, all five died at the watchdog and git log across all five branches shows zero commits. Between fifteen and thirty minutes of work each, and the only surviving trace was the last sentence each had streamed. The cause was environmental, which is exactly why the row exists — an agent cannot prevent the interruption, but it can refuse to hold a round hostage to a single terminal commit.
fields.title: a dispatched agent's entire round lives in its context until one final commit, so any interruption costs all of it

fields.summary: Two comments in a test file assert evidence the round could not have measured and a set it did not enumerate. One claims zero differences where 843 of 846 file modes differ; the other calls a file 'the only other file the copied run executes' where the enumeration finds twenty-four. Both are documentation defects against a round that passed on everything behavioural, and one edit closes both.
fields.title: two comments in tests/test_tree_guard.py assert evidence the round could not have measured and a set it did not enumerate

fields.summary: A host-support test admits four registrations through a gate whose global cap is three, and the runner's own docstring calls the module a known flake without naming the mechanism — which is the problem, because a named flake with an unnamed mechanism is indistinguishable from a real concurrency defect, and this one reads like one. Attributed rather than waved away: the module is red on a pristine archive of the base commit, one run in four under load.
fields.title: test_host_support.py admits four registrations through a gate whose global cap is three, and the runner calls it a flake without naming the mechanism

fields.summary: This test module is now the suite's longest at 48-124 seconds, and its own fix is what put it there. It is NOT a regression and should not be read as one — the round that did it just passed review, and both of the things that cost the time are load-bearing. So the question is not whether the cost is justified but whether it is the right size. The 48-124 second spread is itself the first finding: the module's cost varies 2.6x with machine load.
fields.title: test_tree_guard.py is now the suite's longest module at 48-124s, and its own fix is what put it there

fields.summary: Perry's limiter for concurrent dispatches has a race in it, found while three review rounds were running at once. Reported by a round that deliberately left it outside its own bound, and filed here so the refusal discharges into a row rather than into a sentence in a result document. The limiter is the only thing coordinating concurrent agents on this machine, and five ran at once the night it was found.
fields.title: the dispatch limiter has a race, found while three rounds ran concurrently

fields.summary: A test fixture hard-codes the test-id shape produced by Python 3.11 while its docstring claims it was copied line for line from a real run — and the interpreter this project actually runs is 3.9.6, where the ids collapse to the class name. Counts are unaffected, which is why it was not charged. The part worth knowing beyond this fixture is that two interpreters are in play here and they disagree about test identity.
fields.title: a test-id fixture hard-codes the 3.11 id shape while its docstring says it was copied from a real run, and python3 here is 3.9.6

fields.summary: A module made red only by an unexpected success reports zero failed tests — the exact zero-failures-under-a-red-module shape the fix that shipped argues against, arriving through the one door its guard does not cover. Unreachable today because no test module uses an expected failure. Filed now rather than when somebody writes the first one, because at that point the number will look right and be wrong.
fields.title: a module red only from an unexpected success reports zero failed tests, the exact shape the fix argues against

fields.summary: The header-rule net can see a walk that loses a whole reader DIRECTORY and cannot see one that loses a single reader FILE — and could not before the round that widened it either, so this is the remaining half of an older hole rather than damage from that round. Per-file loss was never expressible in the corpus, whose entries are per-directory.
fields.title: the header-rule net cannot see a walk that loses one real reader file, and could not before TASK-244 either

fields.summary: A round's docstring and its result document both say eight whole-tree scans where the instrumented count is twelve. The delta is right and the cost claim rests on the delta, which is why it was not charged. The four unaccounted scans are one test scanning inside a loop, so the number counts call SITES where the runtime counts CALLS — and that is the same slip the round already fixed once in a neighbouring docstring while leaving this one standing.
fields.title: TASK-244's docstring and result say eight whole-tree scans where the instrumented count is twelve

fields.summary: A markdown code fence disables the paragraph a procedure depends on while the guard checking that paragraph is present stays green. The reviewer filed rather than failed, and the reason is the interesting part: an HTML comment renders as nothing, so a guard staying green over one asserts a reader sees text no reader can see — but fenced prose still renders and is still read. Whoever takes this should decide whether the guard is about BYTES PRESENT or about A READER SEEING, because those two readings diverge here for the first time.
fields.title: a markdown code fence disables the dispatch.md paragraph while its presence guard stays green

fields.summary: A parser's docstring still carries the premise its own round measured false, and now contradicts the corrected copy in perry-lint. The round deliberately left the parser alone, because touching it would have broken the byte-identity carrying an earlier parity result forward without re-earning it — the right call for that round, and it leaves the two docstrings disagreeing with the parser's being the wrong one. Cheap to fix now that the parity no longer needs protecting.
fields.title: scan_spec_escalations' docstring still carries the premise its own round refuted, and now contradicts perry-lint's

fields.summary: A green mutation, filed rather than charged: map one function's error return to True — so nothing is ever reported stale — and all 24 provenance tests still pass. The reason is exact: the test pins only the True and None answers and never the False case, which is the only answer staleness reporting depends on. The shape is worth more than the instance — a three-valued function whose tests pin two values leaves the third free, and here the free one is the whole point of the feature.
fields.title: git_ancestor can be made to never report anything stale and all 24 provenance tests stay green

fields.summary: A result document closes with a false sentence about a lint rule that is deliberate and already recorded. The reviewer checked the round's own alarm and found it half right: the non-monotonicity is real and was reproduced at its source, but it is documented, and the payload DOES record which ids came back clean — so the round's closing claim that nothing records it is false here. Correct the page and open no further row.
fields.title: TASK-304's result page closes with a false sentence about a lint rule that is deliberate and already recorded

fields.summary: A comment names the wrong file as the guard for its own audit wiring: the file it points at is byte-identical to base and contains no occurrence of the term at all. The guard is real and lives elsewhere, so this is a pointer defect rather than a missing guard. Worth a row because a comment that sends a reader to the wrong file to verify a claim costs the next reader exactly the time the comment was meant to save.
fields.title: tests/parallel:371 names the wrong file as the guard for its own audit wiring
TASK-067's population decayed under it — census the write and read paths on today's HEAD and produce the `## Bound` its criteria file never had

fields.summary: A bound claims that names resolve through simple assignment bindings, and that is false for its own f-string clause. NOT URGENT, and that is measured: none of the six shapes exists in the tree today, so the bound is correct about the current tree and wrong only about what it promises for a future one. The risk is the next round trusting the prose. Two citation slips in the same file are to be fixed in the same pass.
fields.title: TASK-067's bound claims names resolve through `NAME = "…"` bindings, and that is false for its own f-string clause

fields.summary: Every task on this board is titled in shorthand that only the agent who wrote it can read. There is already a field meant to fix that -- a short plain-English explanation of what is broken and what changes once it is fixed -- but almost no row fills it in, and most of the ones that do are written in the same shorthand. This makes writing one required, adds a check that refuses the shorthand, and fills in the rows that are blank.
fields.title: Perry has a plain-language field for every task, 90 of 114 open rows leave it empty, and nothing asks for it

fields.summary: Three tests about finding a project's root fail when the whole suite runs at once, but all 23 pass when that file runs on its own. The suspected cause is that agent worktrees sit inside this repository, so a test looking for project roots finds theirs too. The same problem was already fixed in one other test file; this is a second one with it.
fields.title: test_project_root_resolution reddens under the parallel runner while agent worktrees are live — TASK-258's disease in a second module

fields.summary: perry-decide carries its own weaker spelling of the one line-break rule. Its guard tests whether the value has more than one splitlines() element, which a TRAILING newline passes because that call returns a single element for it, while the canonical line_break_at in viewer/tables.py catches it. The comment above the guard records that the pipe half of the same paragraph was fixed two rounds earlier and this half was not.
fields.title: perry-decide guards a line break with a third, weaker spelling

fields.summary: When Perry refuses a write because two rows share an id, it tells you which lines those rows are on. Delete the +1 that turns a zero-based index into a line number and every test still passes, so the refusal would point one line above each row. The equivalent check on the store side does have a test that catches this.
fields.title: duplicate_row_ids' reported line number is off by one and nothing pins it, while its store-side sibling is pinned

fields.summary: Wrapping a path in markdown italics, or just putting an underscore after it, makes the dispatch safety gate stop seeing it. A spec that declares it will edit the claim surface then passes. This is the same kind of failure as the one just fixed -- formatting alone gets you through -- but it lives in a different part of the matcher.
fields.title: markdown italic still clears the claim surface: a trailing underscore is a word character, so the gate's right-edge guard never matches

fields.summary: Perry currently refuses a task summary that has no full stop, or that is shorter than five words. Those are judgements about writing, and the user decided they are the writing agent's responsibility rather than something Python should score. The two rules come out; the checks for a missing summary and for one that just restates the title stay, because those are facts rather than opinions.
fields.title: drop summary-has-no-sentence and summary-is-a-fragment: prose quality is the writing agent's job, not a check's

fields.summary: schema/task-list-contract.md is the READ contract a front-end builds against, and its summary definition still requires 'at least one complete sentence' and still enumerates the structure checks as 'equal to the title, no sentence, under five words'. TASK-330 removed two of those three on 2026-09-03, so the contract now promises a consumer more validation than the tools perform.
fields.title: The task-list contract still defines summary by two rules that no longer exist

fields.summary: TASK-330's own mutation M5 came back GREEN: deleting the NOT CHECKED entry that row was required to add leaves all 3268 tests passing. That register is how a deliberate omission is told apart from an oversight by the next author, so an unpinned one can be deleted silently and the reason for a removal disappears with it.
fields.title: Nothing pins the NOT CHECKED register that records what a predicate declines

fields.summary: The dispatch gate decides whether a round is high-stakes by scanning a spec's prose sections for words the hook names, which cannot tell a citation from a write. Measured on 148 specs: 15 refuse and 5 of those refusals are false positives, including one whose spec header already carries a hand-written note explaining that the gate matched an ordinary English noun. A declared typed field in the spec header would end the whole family rather than narrowing one more character class.
fields.title: Give the escalation gate a typed field to read instead of a spec's prose

fields.next_action: Reconcile status before further work: the account says CLOSED AND VERIFIED, but captured status is not_started. source_of skips vanished untracked files and raises for tracked ones. The separate live-tree rowprobe race belongs to TASK-341; do not treat it as this fix reopening. See perry/evidence/2026-09/TASK-447-next-action-accounts.md#task-334.
fields.summary: tests/test_one_header_rule.py builds its file list once at import time and reads each file later; the read is wrapped in a try that catches SyntaxError but not FileNotFoundError, so a file that disappears between the walk and the read errors the test instead of being skipped. It is the only thing making Perry's full suite red, in 3 of 3 runs tonight, while passing 5 of 5 when the module runs alone.
fields.title: The header-rule guard errors instead of skipping when a file vanishes mid-walk

fields.summary: test_contract_key_parity asserts that conformance.in_progress_with_no_live_run's keys are unobservable without the witness fixture and observable with it. Both halves fail on a clean tree, so the witness project is no longer putting that collection into the state the test needs. It is the only module making Perry's full suite red now that TASK-334 is fixed.
fields.title: Two contract-parity tests fail because the witness cannot make a collection observable

fields.summary: TASK-325 pinned that summary_tokens counts CJK without assuming spaces, and the pin ran through summary-is-a-fragment. TASK-330 removed that rule, so today reverting summary_tokens to str.split() makes a good Chinese summary get refused as summary-repeats-title and every test still passes. TASK-330's own removal was correct; the collateral is that a property the project cares about is now unheld.
fields.title: summary_tokens' CJK behaviour lost its pin when the fragment floor was removed

fields.summary: work/reference/subcommands.md and reference/input-quality.md both say perry-task add refuses a summary with no sentence or under five words. It does not, since TASK-330. TASK-331 fixed the third surface and added a guard, but that guard reads only schema/task-list-contract.md, so it structurally cannot see the two pages an author actually reads before typing the command.
fields.title: Two procedure pages still tell authors the writer refuses summaries it now accepts

fields.summary: TASK-256's round-2 agent saw its own baseline run print a tree-guard line naming a different agent's worktree. Agent worktrees are nested inside this checkout, so a guard meant to prove one run touched nothing is reporting on a sibling's tree. This repository currently carries 49 worktrees, most from finished rounds.
fields.title: A test's tree guard names another agent's worktree, so runs are not isolated from each other

fields.summary: bin/perry-state --escalation-scan decides whether a round is high-stakes by matching a spec's prose against the hook's list, which is Python judging a document's meaning. The user removed it on 2026-09-04. The dispatching agent reads the spec and the hook and makes the call instead, so the deliverable is a written procedure in dispatch.md as much as it is a deletion.
fields.title: Remove the escalation scanner and put the judgement in the dispatch procedure

fields.summary: TASK-263's census found three stale claims while measuring: DESIGN-014 section 5.1's line counts are wrong for all three files it sizes, bin/perry-lint's load_glossary justifies its shape by a tool deleted with USER-910, and bin/perry-task's module docstring says markdown is canonical two paragraphs below its own ADR-007 note saying the opposite. Each was reported rather than fixed because the census row only measures.
fields.title: Three documents in the tree describe a codebase that no longer exists

fields.summary: tests/test_one_choke_point.py creates a real bin/lib/rowprobe.py inside the repository to check that the row-builder guard sees it, and tests/test_one_primitive.py asserts that bin/lib contains exactly one exempt file. Run in parallel the second can see the first's probe and go red for a reason that has nothing to do with what it tests.
fields.title: One test writes a probe file into the live tree while another asserts what is in it

fields.summary: Perry's mutation discipline says to verify a restore with git show <ref>:<path>, and briefs have been writing that ref as main. TASK-339's round did exactly that while main was advancing underneath it, so the restore imported main's newer content into the branch and git diff main looked clean. The instruction is wrong in every brief and every reference page that carries it.
fields.title: Every dispatch brief tells agents to verify restores against a ref that moves

fields.summary: Every spec dispatched on this project for over a week has told agents not to use bin/perry-restore-check and to use git show instead. Its round-3 V4 established that the warning can now narrow to exactly two cases: a round touching the tool itself, and a tree with tracked symlinks. Leaving the blanket warning in place costs every future brief a paragraph and teaches agents to distrust a tool that now works.
fields.title: Narrow the standing warning against perry-restore-check to its two real exclusions

fields.summary: In bin/perry-restore-check, turning the condition that prints the '! self-check' advisory into a constant false removes the line while all 25 tests pass. It is reachable only when the caller passed --allow-modified-self, and no ok field, no check mark and no exit code changes, so it degrades what a reader is told rather than what the tool decides. Found by TASK-256's round-3 V4 reviewer as one of five greens it ran down individually.
fields.title: The self-check advisory line can be deleted with every test still green

fields.summary: TASK-256 round 3 added a sentence to work/reference/review-constraints.md and bin/README.md telling readers to point the live helper at a scratch copy with --root. Measured, that is false for a bare git archive copy, which exits 2 in both directions -- and a git archive copy is what the same paragraph names two sentences earlier. It works for a cp -R copy.
fields.title: A sentence on two shipped pages is false for the copy it names

fields.summary: Both .perry/hook.md and work/state/hook_TEMPLATE.md open the high-stakes section with the sentence that dispatch scans every spec's Files in scope and Deliverable against the list and refuses on a match. TASK-339 deleted that scanner; the judgement is now a written procedure a dispatching agent follows. The paragraph is inside the section that IS the safety gate, and the template ships to every project Perry adopts.
fields.title: The hook's own safety-gate paragraph describes a scanner that no longer exists

fields.summary: In dispatch.md, section 4.4's DOING bullet says any foreign-rooted path appearing anywhere in scope means the round is doing rather than naming, while tell 2 says a path quoted as data is naming. Section 4.5's own worked example needs both readings at once: it states TASK-107 is not refused by the fragments it quotes, yet that bullet as written refuses on exactly those. No precedence is stated, so a reader has to guess.
fields.title: The dispatch procedure's DOING bullet contradicts its own worked example

fields.summary: Classify every call site in viewer/ and in the bin/ tools TASK-263 did not cover into ADR-007's four categories. This is the production half of the sweep and the half ADR-011 Tier B is measured against: 24,005 lines across 21 files, with viewer/parsers.py the largest single target at 4,627 lines and twelve modules importing it.
fields.title: ADR-007 census part 1 — viewer/ and the nineteen remaining bin/ tools

fields.summary: Classify the document handling in tests/, which is 128 files and three quarters of the whole sweep. It is deliberately a separate row because a test that parses a document is usually parsing it to check production code that parses it, so most of these are dependents of part 1 rather than independent debt, and treating them as one population would double-count the work.
fields.title: ADR-007 census part 2 — the 71,158 lines of tests/

fields.summary: Classify the document handling in setup, a 638-line bash script, and in the five modules that read .perry/hook.md. Small, and worth its own row for a specific reason: the word setup in a spec is what the deleted escalation scanner false-refused on for two days, and the hook readers are what USER-916 changed the ownership of.
fields.title: ADR-007 census part 3 — setup and the hook readers

fields.summary: In bin/perry_md_store.py the summary line sums len(report[k]) across the fell-back-to-copying keys. Two of those report dicts keyed by column with an occurrence count as the value, so cells_verbatim {'Owner': 2} is reported as 1 line or cell rather than 2. The number an operator reads to decide whether a render is trustworthy is an undercount, and the same line also documents exit codes 0, 1 and 2 nine lines after exit 3 was introduced.
fields.title: The fell-back-to-copying count reports keys instead of occurrences

fields.summary: An intake item was dropped on 2026-09-01 as covered by TASK-182. It is not covered by TASK-182's gate: appending records to okr.jsonl leaves render --write reporting more stored records while OKR.md is byte-unchanged, and diff exits 0. Only verify catches it, at exit 1, and perry-lint reports it as a warning at exit 0. Found by TASK-182's V4 reviewer, who confirmed the exclusion is argued in that row's own result document and is therefore outside its bound rather than a failure of it.
fields.title: Records appended to okr.jsonl are invisible to the render gate that was said to cover them

fields.summary: TASK-139's V4 reviewer planted twelve mutations and four came back green, all on lines the round wrote and never mutated itself. Two are real behaviour nothing exercises, one is inert, and one is unreachable while a test docstring claims to cover it -- that test passes with the branch disabled, which is the shape this project has failed rounds over.
fields.title: Four lines TASK-139 wrote are untested, and one of them is dead code with a test that claims to cover it

fields.summary: schema/events-list-contract.md:61 states the twenty-six kinds are in the section below, and that section's table now has 27 rows. TASK-139 added the twenty-seventh and the sentence was not updated, because nothing reads that prose and the suite stayed green. It is a READ contract, so the number is a promise to a consumer.
fields.title: The events contract says twenty-six kinds and lists twenty-seven

fields.summary: TASK-139 replaced substring matching over board prose and log lines with declared design_refs edges, which is right, but no backfill has run: all 15 locked designs report impl_refs=0 and no live record carries an edge. So the pending hand-off signal that reads impl_refs discriminates nothing until the backfill lands. The round's result document states this of DESIGN-001 only.
fields.title: Every locked design now reports zero implementation references

fields.summary: tests/test_board_render.py:240 puts a sentinel into a field, restores the field, then asserts the sentinel appears nowhere in the rendered row. The sentinel for status is the ordinary English word dropped, and a task whose next action legitimately uses that word makes the assertion fire. It is red on main right now for exactly that reason, so every baseline measured from here is polluted.
fields.title: A board-render test breaks whenever a row's prose contains its sentinel word

fields.summary: tests/test_host_support's concurrent dispatch-limiter test was measured at a clean base: green in six idle runs and red in six of six under sixteen CPU burners, always under-counting winners rather than exceeding the cap it is named for. It is not flaky in the ordinary sense -- it is a timing assertion that fails whenever the machine is busy, so the next row that adds any subprocess to this suite will be blamed for it.
fields.title: The dispatch-limiter test is load-sensitive, so any row that adds work to the suite trips it

fields.summary: Each of the three source-reading guards does next(n for n in ast.walk(...) if it is a FunctionDef named X). Python binds the LAST top-level definition of a name; ast.walk yields the FIRST. So a duplicate definition placed earlier in the file becomes the guard's target while the real one is what runs, and the guard reports on code nobody executes.
fields.title: Three guards locate a function with next() and never check it is the only one

fields.summary: bin/perry-tasks, bin/perry-okr and bin/perry-config resolve the project root with PERRY_PROJECT overriding --root, the reverse of the order bin/README.md publishes, and two of the three can write a whole file into the project they resolved rather than the one the caller named. tests/test_project_root_resolution.py owns this contract and its docstring names a population that excludes all three.
fields.title: the store family reads --root and then throws it away

fields.summary: perry-tasks checks only argv[0] for -h and perry-okr and perry-config check only argv[1], so perry-tasks render --write --help executes the render instead of printing help, and an unknown flag such as --wrte is a silent no-op that exits 0 because the parser is a set of membership tests over argv.
fields.title: --help runs the command on the three tools that have no argument parser

fields.summary: bin/README.md line 74 says --json and --dry-run mean the same thing everywhere and that --dry-run is how a writer is previewed, but neither string appears in perry-tasks, perry-okr or perry-config, two of which replace a whole file. Either the three writers get both flags or the README stops claiming them.
fields.title: --dry-run and --json are promised for every writer and absent from three

fields.summary: SKILL.md step 3 tells the agent to compute the state in one call to perry-state --json, which on this repository is 186,856 bytes or roughly 47k tokens, and its largest single section is 123KB, while perry-context-budget in the same directory reports that 99.1 percent of this project's token bill is context re-read every turn. There is no small structured read: --dashboard is 1.1KB and text only.
fields.title: the standup's one mandated call is 47k tokens, in the directory that measures context cost

fields.summary: perry-task list --json is 538,134 bytes on this repository and --all --json is 1,683,852 bytes, roughly 420k tokens, which exceeds any context window Perry runs in. The command offers --track and --all and no --limit, no --since and no field selection, so a caller cannot ask for less.
fields.title: perry-task list has no bound, and --all --json does not fit in a context window

fields.summary: Eighteen executables ship with no dispatcher, no perry help and no manifest, so an agent discovers the surface by listing the directory and reading a 20KB prose README whose table cells are paragraphs. Which tools write, what the exit codes mean and which flags exist are each stated in the README and in a help string and checked against the code by nobody.
fields.title: bin/ has no machine-readable index, so every fact about the surface is prose in two places and enforced in none

fields.summary: perry-task answers --help with 160 lines and 10KB whose Usage section starts at line 51, perry-lint with 135 lines and perry-goals with 106, so an agent that wants one subcommand's flags pays roughly 2.5k tokens and reads the tool's history first. The prose is worth keeping; it is in the wrong place.
fields.title: --help is a design paper with the usage block at line 51

fields.summary: perry-task add --help prints the same 10KB global document and perry-tasks build --help runs build, so a tool with roughly thirty subcommands cannot be asked about one of them. Run with no arguments the tools answer four ways: usage and exit 2, full help and exit 0, 187KB of JSON, and a 3.7 second lint.
fields.title: there is no subcommand help, and a bare invocation answers four different ways

fields.summary: The flag table at bin/perry-task:7296 maps --design, so add --design DESIGN-016 is accepted and exits 0, but cmd_add never reads args.design and the record it writes carries design_refs empty. Only design-link at bin/perry-task:4392 ever writes the field, so a caller who used the documented-looking flag believes an edge exists that does not. Found 2026-09-04 while opening this design's own rows: all eight had to be relinked afterwards.
fields.title: perry-task add accepts --design and drops it

fields.summary: Perry's 3,265 tests take 31 minutes of serial machine time because the logic they test lives in executable scripts rather than importable modules. 101 of 124 test modules launch a Perry CLI as a subprocess, 324 times in total, and each launch starts a fresh interpreter that parses perry-task's 7,851 lines and imports parsers.py's 4,627 before reaching the one judgement the test cares about. The median module takes 9.7 seconds; eleven of 103 finish inside a second.
fields.title: The suite has no unit seam: 324 subprocess launches stand in for calling a function

fields.summary: DESIGN-015 section 5.1 lists current_provenance among the kr record's stored fields, but it is computed at read time by bin/lib kr_progress_provenance and appears nowhere in phase/003-linkage.md. Storing it would put a derived value in a canonical store, which contradicts section 5.2's own argument and the Idle precedent in asks.jsonl. TASK-276 declared it as spelled but optional and wrote the conflict into the schema, because amending a locked design is its owner's call rather than an implementing round's.
fields.title: DESIGN-015 stores a field that is derived at read time

fields.summary: TASK-308 shipped a check that reports a spec with no Bound before a round runs against it. It works: it reported TASK-276's spec. I dispatched TASK-276 anyway, because the finding is one of 123 and the output names only the first ten. A check whose true positive is invisible has the same effect as no check, which is what reference/diagnose.md says about a wall of red.
fields.title: The bound check fires on 123 specs, so nobody sees the one that matters

fields.next_action: Couple dispatch/status and reconcile dead agents using the standing 2026-09-04 evidence. Do not reuse the retracted TASK-278 charge (df269b5): another PMO wrote it; the agent's RESULT was accurate. Actor ambiguity is TASK-378, not proof of an agent crossing its boundary. See perry/evidence/2026-09/TASK-447-next-action-accounts.md#task-371.
fields.summary: A dispatch is two independent actions: launching the subagent, and writing the row to in_progress. Nothing joins them, so forgetting the second leaves the board reporting fewer rows running than there are agents. It has happened three times in two days and the user caught the third, when the board said 3 running against 6 live agents.
fields.title: Nothing couples dispatching an agent to marking the row it works on

fields.summary: Every V4 round is told to do destructive mutation work in a scratch copy and then verify the restore with perry-restore-check --root <copy>. That call cannot work: --root repoints the tool's git queries as well as its file paths, so against a git archive copy, which has no git history, it answers '<ref> is not a commit in <copy>'. The procedure Perry hands every reviewer is broken at the step that matters most, and reviewers have been silently falling back to hand-rolled byte comparison instead.
fields.title: perry-restore-check --root cannot verify a git-archive scratch copy — the exact use review-constraints.md recommends

fields.summary: Agents dispatched into separate git worktrees are isolated in the tree but not on disk: they are handed the same session scratchpad path. On 2026-09-07 two V4 reviewers ran concurrently and one overwrote the other's mutation harness while it was in use. The affected round noticed, re-verified its copies against the ref and renamed its harness, so nothing false was reported -- but it noticed by luck, and a round that did not notice would report mutation results produced by another agent's file.
fields.title: Two concurrently dispatched agents share one 'session-specific, isolated' scratchpad and can overwrite each other's files mid-round

fields.summary: The linkage store is parsed by a single comprehension inside one try block, so a single stray line makes the census report linkage-store-unreadable with zero records validated, rather than validating the 120 good records and reporting the one bad line. Two smaller shape defects sit beside it: undeclared extra fields on a record pass silently because the declared field set is used only as a lower bound, and with the stores.declared block absent the census prints 'no linkage.jsonl' for a file that exists. All three fail in the safe direction, never claiming clean, which is why none of them failed the round that found them.
fields.title: One malformed line in linkage.jsonl voids validation of every good record in the file

fields.summary: The linkage store accepts a duplicate edge, a duplicate unlinked entry, and a task carrying both an edge and an unlinked declaration. All three import silently and are reported valid by both the register lint and the store census. DESIGN-015 section 5.2 derives never-asked as the store holding neither an edge nor an unlinked record for a row, so a row holding both is a state that derivation has no reading for -- and P003-O3-KR2 is about to be computed from exactly that derivation.
fields.title: linkage.jsonl has no uniqueness or mutual-exclusion invariant — a task that is both linked and declared unlinked passes every gate

fields.summary: The importer refuses a register declaring a spec version other than linkage: 1, and that refusal works when exercised by hand. But no test feeds it a register with a different version, so disabling the gate entirely does not redden anything. This is the only uncovered branch found in the importer, and it is the branch that protects every future change to the linkage record format from being silently applied to a register written under different rules.
fields.title: The linkage importer's spec-version gate is unguarded — mutating it to if False: leaves the whole suite green

fields.summary: The design.by_status mapping in perry-state's payload comes out in a different key order between runs, because the order follows Python's hash randomisation. TASK-278 hit it while trying to use the full payload as a byte-comparison control and had to fall back to comparing sections. Reproduced at that branch's base, so it predates the row.
fields.title: perry-state's design.by_status key order depends on PYTHONHASHSEED

fields.summary: The event log's actor field carries the literal string agent for 1601 of its records, including every write made by a PMO session through perry-task.
