It does not record which session made a write, nor whether the writer was a PMO steward or a dispatched coding agent. On 2026-09-07 two PMO sessions worked this board concurrently and one read the other's board write as a dispatched agent reaching outside its worktree, then recorded that on two rows and in a commit message, including a charge that the agent's result document was false. The write was the other PMO's and the agent's report was accurate.
fields.title: Every tool-mediated write is stamped actor: agent, so two concurrent PMO sessions cannot tell their writes apart — and one has already misattributed the other's to a dispatched agent

fields.summary: A row parked at review with no verification round ever run is invisible to every check Perry has. The linter reports a row closed at V4 without a verdict eleven times over, and reports nothing at all about a row that simply never leaves review. On 2026-09-07 that was every single row in the column: five rows, all with code already merged to main, none with a verdict document naming it.
fields.title: perry-lint guards the exit from review but not the waiting room — five rows sit at review with merged code and no verdict document, and nothing reports it

fields.summary: The single red module on main is a dogfooding assertion that Perry must not trip its own diagnostic findings. It trips LOAD-03, which counts open decisions queued on the user, currently six. The finding is accurate and the code is not defective, but the consequence is that no engineering change can turn the suite green and every agent measuring a baseline inherits a red it has to re-diagnose from scratch.
fields.title: main cannot have a green suite through code alone — the one red module asserts Perry's user has answered their questions

fields.summary: Three of the four agents dispatched on 2026-09-07 were given a worktree checked out at a 2026-09-02 commit rather than at current main. Each noticed independently and recovered differently, at its own cost. The danger is not the wasted time: a spec's line numbers were measured against that same stale ref, so work built on it matches its spec, passes its own tests, and is wrong about the tree it merges into. REPRODUCED AGAIN 2026-09-10, and the number grew: three review agents dispatched for the DESIGN-016 V4 round were all handed d49964ee, the SAME 2026-09-02 commit as the four on 2026-09-07, now 653 commits behind the branch tip rather than 496. The subject of the review was absent from the tree -- zero of the six SURFACE-declaring tools existed, and the acceptance criteria file did not either. All three stopped at the base gate and produced no verdict, which cost three full dispatches to learn a SHA. THE GATE ONLY WORKED BECAUSE THE DISPATCH PROMPT CARRIED IT: each prompt named the required SHA and said stop if it differs. Nothing in the harness checks this, so a round dispatched without that paragraph would have reviewed a tree with no subject in it. The stale ref is not drifting -- it is pinned at d49964ee across two independent dispatch events eight days apart, which points at a fixed ref rather than a race. The PMO workaround, and the thing to compare a fix against: git worktree add --detach <path> <sha> from the primary checkout, then dispatch a non-isolated agent with that path and an explicit ban on touching the shared checkout.
fields.title: Dispatched agents are handed a worktree 496 commits behind main, and a stale base produces work that looks correct

fields.summary: TASK-281 made P003-O3-KR2 computed from the linkage store and the event log, and wired that into kr_rows so perry-state and perry-goals list both publish it. perry-goals krs builds its KR list through a separate serialiser that reads the register directly, so it publishes None for that KR. It is the surface goals/SKILL.md calls the only one for a phase's key results.
fields.title: Four publishers disagree about a computed KR, and the fourth prints a footer saying no KR is ever measured

fields.summary: Filing a row with --kr writes the edge into the store, which leaves the register document stale and perry-lint reporting drift. The tool named as the way to clear it answers nothing to write, because it checks the store, where the edge already is. The drift is therefore permanent and grows by one row per add --kr, in the one store this phase just finished making a real drift verdict for.
fields.title: add --kr creates a linkage drift no tool can clear, because perry-goals link decides already-linked from the store and the drift is in the document

fields.summary: perry-task add refuses a row without a summary and perry-explain is built on it, but perry-state's board payload omits the key entirely on all 145 rows while perry-task list carries it on 133, and schema/state-schema.json never mentions the field. A consumer following SKILL.md's instruction to read perry-state cannot see a field the writer will not let a row exist without.
fields.title: summary is mandatory to write, reported by the linter, published by one payload and not the other, and declared in no schema

fields.summary: Dispatch briefs now tell agents to keep scratch work inside their own worktree, because two concurrent agents overwrote each other in the shared scratchpad. An agent that does so creates a directory of Perry source copies, which the tree-scanning tests count as real readers, turning test_header_index_is_the_only_fold red. The isolation remedy and the scanning tests are in direct conflict.
fields.title: The scratch-isolation remedy reddens the repo-scanning tests, so an agent obeying its brief breaks the suite it is measured against

fields.summary: In a linkage register, a tasks value written as a block scalar parses to one string ending in a newline. The lookup matches an id exactly, so it never matches, and the edge is lost with no error anywhere. The register declares a link that no KR counts, no attribution sees, and no check reports as missing.
fields.title: A pipe-written tasks value is a hard lint error and, separately, resolves to nothing in a reader that never consults the linter

fields.summary: perry-goals warns on every write that moves an assertion date, naming each affected KR, because the real fix is behind a safety gate and naming it is what stops the problem being discovered as a silent number months later. The linkage-write path built today reads the same field for the same purpose and reports nothing; it re-dated 115 records in one run in silence. The defect was inherited and the disclosure was not.
fields.title: A mitigation that lives in one writer's body was not inherited by the next writer that read the same field

fields.summary: ADR-017 chose to complete the KR id migration so one grammar serves both levels, and records that it proposes rather than performs. The overall ids were never renamed: OKR.md still carries all 20 in the old form and the new form appears nowhere. The migration is not a substitution, because the reader regex requires an id to start with KR or P and the new overall form starts with O, so renaming the data before widening the readers makes 20 live ids unreadable.
fields.title: ADR-017 is decided and unperformed: 20 overall KR ids still use the old grammar, and the new one is rejected by the readers

fields.summary: Perry carries 1.96 lines of test per line of code for a stdlib tool whose product is 8,469 lines of prose, and the largest test modules look like guards on how the repository is written rather than on what Perry does. This round measures that split per module and reports what each convention guard would cost to lose. It deletes nothing; deletion is the user's decision after reading it.
fields.title: ADR-018 part C — classify the 73,863-line test suite by what a failure would mean, before anything is deleted

fields.summary: viewer/parsers.py parses the Linked OKR header of every design document into a dataclass field and no code anywhere reads it. Renaming one to a grammar nothing resolves leaves perry-lint at zero errors, the diagnose finding set byte-identical and the dangling-reference list empty. The line that says which goal a design serves is decorative, and it is the mirror of the implementation-reference edge that TASK-355 and TASK-282 are about.
fields.title: A design's Linked OKR line is parsed into a field nothing reads, so a design can name a KR that does not exist and every instrument stays green

fields.summary: perry-task add --kr with --actor goals is a combination the help text documents, and it appends an edge record stamped with a caller-supplied lane that a test forbids. The linkage writer is append-only with no retraction, so nothing Perry ships can withdraw the record. The root cause is that the lane is caller-supplied on the add path and a hardcoded constant on the import path, while the test reads the field as if only the importer wrote it.
fields.title: A documented flag combination writes a linkage record that permanently reddens the suite, and the writer has no retraction

fields.summary: The V4 that passed row C recorded three findings about the round's instruments rather than the product. The Bound states an unbounded set of key spellings as a count of two and omits a whole placement the parser handles; one mutation survived green because the blank-line skip has no assertion behind it; and the sweep for confounding references covered board cells and stores but not evidence documents. None was the verdict, and none is nothing.
fields.title: TASK-278's Bound undercounts its own set, a blank-line skip is unasserted, and the confound sweep misses evidence documents

fields.next_action: Correct the shipped OKR template's six retired KR forms and check test_shipped_vocabulary pins the new grammar; update or add the matching assertion. ADR-017's data rename is separate. Do not sweep the other 420 historical occurrences in evidence/journal/snapshots. See perry/evidence/2026-09/TASK-447-next-action-accounts.md#task-393.
fields.summary: ADR-017 renamed 136 occurrences across this project's data and corpus, but goals/state/OKR_TEMPLATE.md still carries six ids in the old form. That template is what a new project's OKR.md is built from, so every fresh Perry project would be created in the grammar this repository just retired, undoing the migration one project at a time.
fields.title: The shipped OKR template still mints the retired KR grammar, so a new project starts in the form ADR-017 just removed

fields.summary: The KR counts a row as answered if its add event carries a KR or if an unlinked record with via add exists for it. The second shape has no writer anywhere, so a row that genuinely serves no KR can only stay silent and be counted as never asked. This builds the writer DESIGN-015 section 5.5 assigns to the work lane and never implemented.
fields.title: add has no way to declare a row serves no KR, so the honest answer is unrecorded and DoD item 5's second half has no writer

fields.summary: The renderer rebuilds OKR.md from the store by matching each row to its record on the Id cell. A hand-edited id therefore matches no record, and render passes the line through verbatim rather than restoring it. diff still reports the drift, so the two tools disagree about whether the file can be put back in line, and nothing states that limit.
fields.title: perry-okr diff reports an id drift that render --write cannot repair, because render matches rows by the id that drifted

fields.summary: aiMark round 7 found this the expensive way: --summary became required on add, and the first thing that told aiMark was a create being refused in a user's face. Nothing on the write path publishes what a verb requires, so a consumer cannot assert its argv against Perry before shipping. The read side solved this with contract version strings and semantics; the write side has neither.
fields.title: perry-task has no published write contract, so a newly required flag reaches a consumer as a refusal at runtime

fields.summary: aiMark asks for perry-goals/list 2.4 with a semantics entry naming krs[].id, okr.objectives[].krs[] and unlinked_task_ids as the fields whose values moved. Their argument is stronger than the 2.2 precedent: 2.2 changed a timestamp format and a naive parser broke loudly, while ADR-017 changed what an id can be, and a consumer holding KR-O1.1 gets no parse error at all — it gets nothing. A minor is correct because no key was added, removed or retyped.
fields.title: ADR-017 changed an identifier's value space and perry-goals/list stayed at 2.3, so a consumer joining on a stored KR id gets a silent miss

fields.summary: aiMark's rule, stated so Perry can hold it: when --json is passed, stdout is the whole answer and stderr carries only what a human running the tool by hand needs. The no-KR warning add writes today is a second copy of a fact the payload already carries as register_store null and linkage_record null, which is the exact duplication this correspondence is about. Not exit codes — a create that succeeded is exit 0, and encoding succeeded-but there would break every consumer checking code non-zero in the other direction.
fields.title: an advisory a program must act on is a payload field, not a stderr line, and add still writes one under --json

fields.summary: Longest-first scheduling in tests/parallel reads this file to decide worker order, and it is off by up to 62x in one direction and 5x in the other against a real run: test_parallel_runner 62x, test_one_header_rule 12.8x, test_one_choke_point 7.4x, test_md_store 0.2x. 101 modules are marked unstamped and 11 were never measured at all. Until the file describes a run that happened, every later timing claim in this series is unmeasurable.
fields.title: tests/durations.json describes no run that has happened, so no speedup can be attributed and no regression can be seen

fields.summary: test_tree_guard costs 127.5 CPU-seconds — more than half the 245s wall on its own — because each of its 25 cases unpacks a whole repository copy. It asserts nothing about a writer. The guard itself must stay armed on every run; only its self-tests move to a slow path. Measured 2026-09-08 on 86dafda7 at 8 workers.
fields.title: the suite's most expensive module tests the suite's own guard, at 5.1s per test, and it sets the makespan floor

fields.summary: CPython writes no .pyc for a script run as __main__, so perry-task's 8294 lines are recompiled on all 2088 calls a suite run makes — 17.5ms each, and 12.0ms for perry-lint, 6.1ms for perry-goals. Of a 121ms perry-task list, 103ms is startup before any work. Loading the body once as a module and calling main(argv) costs 33ms once then 4.0ms per call, verified against the real payload rather than a stub. This is the only item that also makes every agent and user command faster, not just the suite.
fields.title: every bin/ entrypoint is recompiled on every invocation because an extensionless __main__ is never bytecode-cached

fields.summary: The pattern throughout the product-behaviour modules is a per-test temp project built by shelling out once per row. In test_track_move 50 of 146 calls are add creating fixture rows — 35 percent of the module's time before a single assertion. Those calls need no process boundary: loading the tool once per worker and calling main(argv) takes the same call from 121ms to 4.0ms. Largest single win in the series, and it carries V5 because it changes how tests execute and this runner has already reported 1207 tests against 1287 while looking like a win.
fields.title: class-A tests build every fixture row by spawning the CLI, so 386 CPU-seconds go to process startup before any assertion runs

fields.summary: USER-916 deleted --escalation-scan on exactly this ground after five rounds ended with the measurement that formatting alone flipped the verdict in both directions. That ruling was applied to one gate and not its neighbours. test_heading_defines asks whether a heading argues about an id or defines it; test_procedures_call_the_tool decides in 1141 lines whether a procedure step is teaching a hand edit; test_shipped_vocabulary judges whether a string is something a user could type. Those are agent judgements. The deterministic half stays in Python: test_pointers_resolve, test_router_budget, test_reference_pages_are_reachable and the lint half of test_glossary compute reachability, byte counts and graph edges, which is arithmetic.
fields.title: four test modules use a regex to judge meaning, which ADR-007 decision 3 already ruled the Python layer never does

fields.summary: A test named test_the_risk_cleared_on_2026_08_16_no_longer_counts has to be edited every time the real board moves, which is churn the product never asked for — and a red that means nothing trains everyone to skim reds. Saves no wall time; this is a churn item and mixing it into a speed round is how the speed round stops being measurable. CENSUS RUN 2026-09-10 AND ALL THREE FIGURES IN THE TITLE ARE WRONG, IN DIFFERENT DIRECTIONS. Not 36 modules: 19 name (PERRY_HOME|ROOT)/'perry', 53 reach this repo's own perry/ or .perry/ by any route across 189 sites, and 25 modules / 63 test methods actually have live data flowing into an assertion. Not 614 dates: 656 ISO dates counting comments and docstrings, 531 as code literals, and only 5 inside a live-reading test method, of which 1 was a live-board expected value. Not 191 ids: 3267 raw, 1360 code literals, 8 inside a live-reading test method, and ZERO were live-board expected values. UNDER A BOUNDED CRITERION -- a date or id literal in code, docstrings and comments excluded, inside a test method whose data reaches it from this repository's own perry/ tree -- the real set is 12 SITES IN 8 MODULES, all of which were read. ONE WAS CHURN AND IS CONVERTED; TEN ARE LOAD-BEARING and are listed with a reason each. So the row's premise holds and its scale does not: this was a 1-site problem wearing a 600-site title, and the title is what made it look like a phase of work. THE FINDING UNDER THE FINDING: tests/live_state_expectations.py exists to catch exactly this class and MISSES THE ROW'S OWN HEADLINE EXHIBIT, through two blind spots its docstring does not name -- taint does not cross setUp into test methods, and a comprehension over a tainted iterable is not tainted. With both closed the sweep finds exactly one new finding tree-wide. The guard was NOT changed: that is a mechanism change with its own baseline fixture and wants its own row.
fields.title: 36 test modules assert against live project state, pinning 614 dates and 191 ids that go red when the board moves rather than when code breaks

fields.summary: TASK-402 converted a shared helper reaching 21 modules, another reaching 7, plus test_goals_writer and test_diagnose, and verified every round by comparing id sets. An identical id set proves the conversion changed no outcome; it says nothing about whether the assertions would notice a regression. This project's own rule is that a gate is not green until it has been shown able to go red, and the V5 sign-off on TASK-402 excludes this by name rather than implying it. The same gap exists on the ADR-019 linkage half, which was never mutated either.
fields.title: four in-process conversion rounds shipped without a single mutation, so nothing shows those tests would still go red

fields.summary: The command bin/README.md names as the recovery path printed 'rendered from 399 stored record(s)' and exit 0 after restoring none of 151 deleted rows.
fields.title: render --write reports a recovery it did not perform

fields.summary: The except covered only project_lock, so a Refused raised deeper reached the caller as a Python traceback where the lane tool printed one line.
fields.title: perry-tasks lets Refused escape as a traceback

fields.summary: Eighteen executables with no dispatcher, so bin/README.md is the only discovery path and it is measurably behind. Decision 5 chose declaration plus one thin reader.
fields.title: no single command lists the bin/ surface

fields.summary: risk-add against risks-build for the same register: track is data read from a store while register is four hard-coded prefixes over stores the schema already declares.
fields.title: the store family spells one verb four times, once per register

fields.summary: The most prominent write example in the file teaches a call that add refuses, and the no-LLM claim is contradicted by a tool that shells out to codex.
fields.title: bin/README.md states eight things the tools no longer do

fields.summary: FOUND BY V4 ROUND 4, DESIGN-016, AND REPRODUCED ON ALL SIX TOOLS AT ONCE. Direction B -- a flag SURFACE declares that no code reads -- was planted on all six tools in one mutation and 3440 tests stayed at baseline. perry-task start --rung V4 exits 0, prints 'wrote TASK-001 (start)' and stores rung=None: the accepted-and-silently-dropped defect DESIGN-016 section 1.4 says the declaration was bought to remove. Direction A -- code reads a flag the declaration does not carry -- is guarded on perry-task only, by an AST walk; dropping --wip from perry-config track's declared flags while bin/perry-config:289 still reads it left the suite at baseline, which is the round-1 regression shape reproducible today. THE GUARD THAT EXISTED IS A HAND-WRITTEN TABLE OF TEN (tool, sub, flag) ROWS AT tests/test_bin_surface.py ELSEWHERE, against a negative space the same reviewer measured at 1277 pairs. 134afea6 closed BOTH directions for perry-task by inverting the AST walk already there, and left the other five because each has a different dispatch shape: perry-tasks and perry-config are if-chains, perry-okr runs perry_md_store whose flags are declared in a FUNCTION rather than a literal, and perry-state and perry-diagnose declare zero subcommands so their direction-B question is tool-level rather than per-subcommand. WHAT THE REVIEWER ALSO ESTABLISHED, so this row need not re-derive it: the negative space is clean today -- 1277 probes, 0 accepted -- so this is a guard against tomorrow, not a live defect. perry-config track --mode specifically is intact.
fields.title: the declaration is checked both ways on perry-task alone; the other five tools are unguarded in both directions

fields.summary: FOUND BY V4 ROUND 4, DESIGN-016. TWO DEFECTS IN ONE SNIPPET, BOTH LATENT AND BOTH DOCUMENTATION-ONLY, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A ROW AND NOT A FAIL. (1) change['version'] > TESTED_MINOR_STR is a STRING compare, so '1.5' > '1.18' is true and a consumer pinned at 1.18 is warned about an OLDER change -- the exact comparison the page's own semantics[].version row warns against, 'never as a float', string compare working only 'against the same-shaped string'. (2) if (major, minor) > max(SUPPORTED) with SUPPORTED = {(1,18),(2,0)} makes any 1.x minor drift unreportable, because (1,19) > (2,0) is false. NOTHING EXECUTES THE SNIPPET. The reviewer DID execute the OTHER snippet on that page -- the rule-1 version gate -- and it is correct: it accepts 2.0 against a live payload, accepts 1.18, rejects 3.0. So the page is half-verified and this is the unverified half. The tool ships 2.0, so no consumer is being misled today. RELATED: the changelog guard on the same page was wrong until 2ba2c565 (range(minor+1) demanded twenty headings at 1.19 and one at 2.0) and round 4 confirmed the no-gaps-per-major replacement with four independent mutations, all red.
fields.title: the contract page's rule-3 snippet compares minors as strings, so a consumer is warned about older changes and blind to newer ones

fields.summary: FOUND BY V4 ROUND 4, DESIGN-016. grep -rn 'open_total|closed_total' tests/ returns NOTHING across 3440 tests. Setting open_total = total makes perry-task list report open_total 404 / closed_total 0 on a store that is truly 156/248, print the wrong figure on stderr too, and leave the whole suite at baseline. NOT A FAIL and the reviewer was right not to call it one: the values are correct at HEAD, and neither DESIGN-016 goal 6 nor the round's criterion 6 names them -- criterion 6 asks that the payload SAY how many rows exist beyond the bound, which bound.total and bound.truncated do and which ARE asserted. But schema/task-list-contract.md tells dashboards to render exactly these two fields, so a regression here is consumer-visible and silent.
fields.title: bound.open_total and bound.closed_total are published to dashboards and asserted by nothing

fields.summary: COST TWO OF THREE V4 REVIEWERS A DETOUR ON 2026-09-10 AND WILL COST THE NEXT ONE THE SAME. tests/test_resume.py TestStaleRuns.test_a_fresh_run_is_not_stale is red and pre-existing: it is byte-identical at 4ebc0693 and one reviewer confirmed it red there by extracting that commit with git archive, the other by re-running it alone. Neither could attribute it without doing that work, because the round's declared baseline named only the two test_contract_key_parity tests. The mechanism is a clock: schema stale_run_days is 30 against a fixture stamped a fixed number of days ago, so the test measures the distance between a hard-coded date and today. THE REVIEW PROTOCOL ALREADY HAS THE RIGHT WORD FOR THIS -- an incomplete exhibit is the author's to fix BEFORE dispatch -- and the criteria file for DESIGN-016 now names all three reds. That is a patch on one round; this row is the test. See also the memory note re-run a red module alone before attributing it: this is the fourth clock- or order-dependent red on this board.
fields.title: test_resume's stale-run test is clock-dependent and red on main, and it is not in any declared baseline

fields.summary: ASKED BY AIMARK 2026-09-09, reading perry-goals/list/3.0 against Perry's own project, and the consequence is visible on their page. P003-O3-KR2 is the most rigorously measured row in the register -- bin/lib section same_action_linkage recomputes it from linkage.jsonl and .perry/events.jsonl on every read, current 43.333333333333336, provenance measured with numerator 13 and denominator 30 -- and it is the ONLY row aiMark shows nothing for, because it draws a bar only when target and current are both numbers. That is Perry's own rule: contract 2.0 removed progress because Perry cannot tell which direction a KR runs, and the contract page says only the consumer draws the bar. So aiMark obeys and displays nothing. Phase objective O3 has exactly this one KR, so it renders as 'nobody wrote down what done would mean' beside a number Perry recomputes from two event logs on every read, next to O1 at 100%. THE TARGET EXISTS AND IS PROSE: the first three words of metric are 'Target 100%.' AIMARK OFFERED TWO SHAPES AND SAID IT CANNOT PICK, BECAUSE PICKING IS INFERRING: (a) target 100, current stays a percentage, additive, a minor; (b) target 30 / current 13, the count form every other phase KR uses, but it retypes what current MEANS on this row and needs a semantics entry. THE PMO RECOMMENDS (a), ON A FACT AIMARK DID NOT HAVE: this KR's denominator is not fixed. same_action_linkage computes it as 'the rows that were asked' -- the main-track rows whose own add event carries a kr key -- so it GROWS every time a row is opened during phase 003. Under (b) the target would move under the KR, and a target that changes when someone opens a row is a denominator, not a target. The other phase KRs are counts because their targets are fixed counts (6 stores declared); this one is not the same shape. Under (a) the target is 100 and fixed, which is what was authored, and the moving denominator stays where it belongs, in current_measurement. ONE THING TO SETTLE WHILE DOING IT: 43.333333333333336 is float noise in a published payload; decide the precision and say it on the page.
fields.title: a computed KR publishes current with no target, so the best-measured row in the register renders as unwritten

fields.summary: DESIGN-022 phase A, widening this row. Its original finding stands and is now answered: a hand-measured zero and a template zero were byte-identical because nothing recorded a measurement as such. linkage.jsonl gains two appended record kinds, check (kr, okr_version, id, direction, target, baseline) and measurement (kr, okr_version, check, value, asserted_at, evidence, computed), authorized by USER-937. perry_store holds the two ordering rules (a re-declared check supersedes from its declared_at; a check's current value is its latest measurement). bin/lib gains one derivation beside kr_progress_provenance: per check state/met/fraction, per KR the worst state and all-met, per Objective counts with stretch excluded and no mean. perry-goals/list gains checks[], state, met and fraction as a minor version.
fields.title: DESIGN-022 A — KR checks and measurements are records, and met is derived on read

fields.summary: A CLOSED ROW WHOSE VERIFICATION DID NOT VERIFY, FOUND BY V4 ROUND 5 AND NOT BY THE ROUND THAT CLOSED IT. TASK-361 is DESIGN-016 A3, --dry-run and --json on every writer. Round 4 PASSed it and the PMO closed it at V4 on 2026-09-10. Round 5 then disabled the dry-run gate at bin/perry-tasks:234 and the FULL suite stayed green while perry-tasks write --from-board --dry-run rewrote its store and printed 'wrote'; the same at bin/perry-config:117 rewrote .perry/config.jsonl while printing 'Nothing was written'. The test round 4 relied on, test_dry_run_changes_no_bytes_anywhere, minted every store in setUp and then compared bytes -- so the non-dry-run twin was a byte no-op and the comparison could not distinguish a dry run from a real one for 8 of the 41 writing subcommands. Its reached>=2 guard counted commands that EXITED 0, not commands that would have changed bytes. THE GAP IS ALREADY CLOSED IN CODE, 1789af8a: each command now disturbs its own side first and carries its own control, and perry-config gained the dry-run sweep it never had. Both mutations are red. SO THIS ROW IS BOOKKEEPING, NOT WORK -- and it is filed rather than fixed silently because the PMO closed a row on a verification that did not hold, and the board currently says TASK-361 passed V4 without saying what that PASS covered. A SECOND DISCREPANCY THE SAME REVIEWER FOUND: the criteria file's row map assigns criterion 4 to TASK-361, and round 5's dispatch routed criterion 4a to TASK-360, so the finding was charged to TASK-360's verdict. Whoever reconciles this should make the two agree.
fields.title: TASK-361 was closed on a V4 PASS whose test could not have failed for 8 of the 41 writing subcommands

fields.summary: FOUND BY TASK-404's CENSUS, 2026-09-10, AND IT IS THE SHARPER HALF OF THAT ROW. tests/live_state_expectations.py is the guard against a test using Perry's own live board as its EXPECTED VALUE. It reports 2 findings, both adjudicated false positives, and it did not report test_the_risk_cleared_on_2026_08_16_no_longer_counts -- the exhibit TASK-404's own title is built on. TWO BLIND SPOTS, BOTH VERIFIED AGAINST A PROBE AND BY RE-RUNNING THE SHIPPED SWEEP WITH EACH CLOSED: (1) taint(fn) walks ONE function, so self.text = (PERRY_HOME/'perry'/'BOARD.md').read_text() in setUp is invisible to every test method in the class; (2) a comprehension over a tainted iterable is judged not-live, so cleared = [r for r in parsed if r.resolved] is clean even when parsed is not. Neither is named in the module's docstring. WITH BOTH CLOSED THE SWEEP FINDS EXACTLY ONE NEW FINDING ACROSS THE WHOLE TREE -- tests/test_risks.py:507, which TASK-404 has since converted -- so closing them costs almost nothing today and is worth doing while that is true. NOT DONE UNDER TASK-404 ON PURPOSE: changing the guard means re-recording its baseline fixture, which other agents may be holding, and a guard change deserves its own round rather than riding along inside a conversion.
fields.title: live_state_expectations misses the class it exists to catch: taint does not cross setUp, and a comprehension over a tainted iterable is clean

fields.summary: FOUND 2026-09-10 ON TASK-360. perry-lint reports review-rounds-exhausted after 2 FAILs, and the rule behind it is sound: a row that has failed twice is failing on a PRINCIPLE nobody has picked, and each further round re-derives it differently. TASK-360's two FAILs are not that. Round 4 failed it on criterion 2, help from a non-first argument position on perry-restore-check -- worst outcome exit 2 and a line naming --help, no wrong answer and no data loss. Round 6 failed it on criterion 3, a positional that is accepted, dropped, and reported as a success. DESIGN-016-spec.md's section 'What a criterion may do to a row', added 2026-09-10 and committed, grades criterion 2b as ROW and criterion 3 as FAIL -- so by the bar that now governs this row, it has failed ONCE. THE COUNTER CANNOT SEE THAT because it counts verdict blocks and not the criterion each was charged against. THIS IS NOT AN ARGUMENT FOR LOOSENING THE GUARD. The guard fired correctly on TASK-362, which really has failed four rounds on FAIL-grade criteria, and the ask it demanded -- USER-924 -- is a real fork worth the user's time. It is an argument that the grading the criteria file introduced should reach the counter, otherwise a round charged at the wrong rung goes on costing after the record has been corrected. WHAT THE FIX NEEDS: a verdict block does not currently name the criterion it failed on. Either it gains that field, or the counter reads the criteria file's grade table by criterion id. The first is a contract change to work/reference/review.md section 3; the second couples the linter to one project's spec file and is probably wrong.
fields.title: review-rounds-exhausted counts a FAIL the criteria file later regraded below the line

fields.summary: FOUND 2026-09-10 AND IT IS RED ON MAIN RIGHT NOW. bin/perry-diagnose:335 ANSWERED = re.compile(r'\b(answered|resolved|closed|done|decided|已回答|已解决|已决定)\b') is searched against the WHOLE BOARD LINE, so any of those words appearing in the QUESTION marks the ask answered. Measured on USER-924, filed today: its text contains 'round 6, the PAIRING resolved each expectation through the very path it was checking', diagnose matches 'resolved', and open_decisions_by_register.queue reports 0 while one ask is pending. THIS IS TWO IMPLEMENTATIONS OF ONE RULE, the shape this repository keeps finding in itself. viewer/parsers.py:2094 already has _ASK_STILL_OPEN = ('pending','waiting','open','—','-') and ask_is_answered(status_cell) at :2097, which reads the STATUS CELL. perry-diagnose does not call it and scans prose instead -- which ADR-007 decision 3 forbids in as many words: Python does not parse document semantics. IT HAS BEEN BROKEN THE WHOLE TIME AND NOTHING COULD SEE IT. The reconciliation test asserts diagnose and perry-task agree, and 0 == 0 held for weeks because every ask in the queue was answered. It went red the first time a pending ask existed. That is not a flaky test; it is a test that finally got an input. NOTE THE SECOND-ORDER RISK: the fix must not simply widen the regex. Perry-task writes 'pending' and the fixture writes 'open', and the shared predicate already knows both -- calling it is the fix; teaching a second copy the same words is how there come to be three.
fields.title: perry-diagnose reads the whole board line for the word answered, so an ask whose question contains resolved counts as answered

fields.summary: SELF-REPORTED BY THE AGENT THAT DID IT, 2026-09-10, WHICH IS THE ONLY REASON IT IS KNOWN. Drafting specs for four rows, it redirected a baseline to scratchpad/baseline.txt while a sibling agent in scratchpad/fixA was writing the same path; on seeing the wrong tree name in the output it ran pkill -f 'tests/run'. fixA's log shows 'Terminated: 15'. THE BLAST RADIUS IS WIDER THAN THE AGENT KNEW: ListAgents shows seven interactive peer sessions on this machine at the time, two of them other Perry sessions (perry-73, perry-84). A pattern kill on 'tests/run' reaches every session's suite, not just this one's subagents, and none of them would see a reason -- they would see a run that died. FOURTH COLLISION OF THE SAME ROOT CAUSE, all four in two days: V4 round 4's r4b and r4c both wrote scratchpad/baseline.txt and one clobbered the other mid-run; round 5 the same; round 6 the same; and now a clobber that escalated into a process kill. Three times it cost a re-measurement. This time it cost another agent's work. TWO FIXES AND THEY ARE DIFFERENT SIZES. (1) work/reference/review-constraints.md already forbids git checkout / stash / reset / clean by name, and the reasoning transfers verbatim -- each one can destroy work that is not yours and not recoverable. It does not mention signals. Add pkill, killall and kill -9, with the reason: on a shared machine a pattern kill has no way to tell your process from someone else's, and the agent that runs one cannot see who else was working. (2) The dispatch side is the actual root cause: every prompt in this session handed out one scratchpad directory and told the agent to namespace inside it, which is advice, not isolation. A private path per agent removes the collision instead of asking four agents in a row to remember.
fields.title: an agent ran pkill -f 'tests/run' on a shared machine and killed a sibling's suite; the scratchpad has now collided four times

fields.summary: FOUND BY TASK-394's V3 ROUND 2026-09-10, DRIVEN RATHER THAN REASONED: the reviewer killed a real add with -9 after BOARD.md and before the event append, and measured the result. The row and its unlinked declaration land TOGETHER -- that half is correct and is what the round was checking. What the lost add event costs is the KR: bin/lib section same_action_linkage derives its denominator from the rows whose own add event carries a kr key, so a row with no add event leaves BOTH the numerator and the denominator. The KR reads 0/0 with current None, and no desync detector names the row. IT DEFLATES RATHER THAN INFLATES, which is why the round reported it instead of charging it -- a KR that under-counts is not a KR that lies about being met, and TASK-394's spec puts KR computation out of scope. THE REASON IT IS WORTH A ROW ANYWAY: store_edge_without_event already exists as the mirror check on the other side, so the shape is one this codebase treats as worth detecting; the same crash window on the other register would be reported and this one is not. AND THE NUMBERS ARE LIVE: perry/linkage.jsonl holds 13 records with via add and attribution.declared_unlinked is 110, so the derivation this affects is in production use, not hypothetical.
fields.title: a crash between the board write and the event append removes a row from both halves of P003-O3-KR2, and no desync detector names it

fields.summary: FOUND BY V4 ROUND 7 AND MEASURED ACROSS ALL TWENTY EXECUTABLES, 2026-09-10. With a subcommand lead each tool accepts, 8 of 20 answered an undeclared flag wrongly. FIVE WERE FIXED IN THE SAME PASS because they write: perry-goals, perry-decide, perry-knowledge, perry-dispatch-limit, and perry-update-check whose bad-invocation exit went 1 to 2. THREE ARE LEFT AND ALL THREE ARE READ-ONLY, which is why they are a row and not a FAIL -- their worst outcome is a flag silently ignored on a command that writes nothing: perry list --xyzzy exits 0; perry-detect-host --xyzzy exits 0 AND PRINTS ITS ANSWER, so a caller reading stdout gets a real host name from an invocation it got wrong; perry-explain TASK-001 --xyzzy exits 0. A FOURTH, DIFFERENT SHAPE: perry-goals krs <positional> refuses at exit 1 rather than 2 -- a refusal code where a bad-invocation code belongs, which criterion 10a is about because callers branch on it. THE THREE ARE NAMED IN A STILL_DROPS TABLE WITH A TEST THAT GOES RED WHEN ONE IS FIXED, so a fourth tool joining them fails the suite and fixing one is a one-line deletion. That is the shape review.md asks for -- a measured, listed remainder rather than an open search.
fields.title: three read-only tools accept an undeclared flag and exit 0; perry-goals krs refuses a positional at exit 1 not 2

fields.summary: THE READING THE USER DID NOT TAKE ON USER-924, filed so it is a decision with a home rather than an assumption. TASK-362 asked what independent source of truth the --compact projection test has. MEASURED ANSWER: none. tests/test_compact_payload.py reads no store file and no schema -- grep for config.jsonl, okr.jsonl, linkage.jsonl and state-schema returns nothing. --json is the reference on both sides of every comparison in that module, and BOTH payloads come from one build(). If build() reads the wrong source for a field, the two agree, the standup shows the wrong number, and every test in the module passes. THE USER CHOSE READING 1 -- a projection is checked for consistency over its declaration, and the value underneath belongs to the function producing it -- ON A FACT THAT MAKES THIS ROW SMALLER THAN IT LOOKS: --json is already pinned to the schema by a different module, tests/test_wip_and_stages.py:40, and round 7 measured the composition holding (default_stages_for returning [] is green on the compact module and red on the full suite). SO THIS ROW IS NOT 'the payload is unverified'. It is: the pinning is by composition across modules and nobody has enumerated which sections are covered that way and which are not. The deliverable is that enumeration plus a pin for whatever it finds bare -- not a rewrite of the projection tests, which reading 1 settles. CORRECTION 2026-09-10, TO THE CITATION THIS ROW AND USER-924'S ANSWER BOTH REST ON. Both say --json is pinned to the schema at tests/test_wip_and_stages.py:40. That line binds SCHEMA = json.loads(state-schema.json) AND NOTHING EVER READS IT -- grep returns one hit, the assignment. The pin that actually exists is at :83, :90 and :96: a HAND-WRITTEN copy of the queue vocabulary inside the test bodies. THE DECISION IS UNAFFECTED and the composition still holds -- round 8 truncated default_stages_for at bin/perry-state:543 and test_a_blank_stages_cell_reports_the_modes_vocabulary went red, which is what USER-924's reading 1 rests on. BUT THE DIFFERENCE IS REAL AND BELONGS IN THIS ROW: a hand-written vocabulary is a second author, which is the right shape and is why it catches the mutation -- and it is NOT a read of the schema, so it can drift from the schema without anything noticing. That is a narrower guarantee than the one the decision was recorded against, and it makes this row's enumeration more valuable rather than less: whoever does it should count how many sections are pinned by a schema READ versus by a hand-written copy, because those two are not the same promise.
fields.title: no test compares a --compact or --json value against the store files or the schema, so a wrong build() agrees with itself

fields.summary: FOUND BY TASK-356's FIRST V4 ROUND, 2026-09-10, AND IT SETTLES A QUESTION THE ROW ITSELF LEFT OPEN. The docstring says USER-916 renders status: dropped on the live board today. It does not. USER-916 lives in perry/asks.jsonl, not tasks.jsonl; it renders in the ASK table and its status cell reads 'answered 2026-09-04: 答复…'. The row's own PMO note had said this could not be reproduced on main and left it unsettled -- it is now settled, and the answer is that the citation is wrong. THE CLAIM THE CITATION SUPPORTS IS TRUE AND HAS A FAR BETTER WITNESS: 36 rows in tasks.jsonl hold status 'dropped'. So this is a swap, not a rewrite. WHY IT WAS FILED AND NOT FAILED: review.md section 2 routes a false claim in a docstring to a row rather than a FAIL -- nobody executes a docstring -- and TASK-356's spec puts it out of scope explicitly. The round respected both and recorded the finding instead of spending the verdict on it. WHILE THERE, low value and noted rather than filed separately: the same docstring's census numbers have drifted with the board (145 to 154 rendered rows, dropped collisions 7 to 4, and V6 now collides in 1 row, which the docstring itself predicted would happen the day a V6 existed). That drift is EXPECTED and is precisely why the test is a construction rather than a scan -- but a number meant to read as a measurement should carry its date and ref.
fields.title: a board-render test cites USER-916 for a status it does not carry, and the true witness is 36 rows away

fields.summary: FOUND BY V4 ROUND 8, 2026-09-10, AND IT IS THE FIX FOR ROUND 7 BITING BACK. bin/perry-restore-check:193-195 reaches lib.empty_root_error through a DEFERRED import -- sys.path.insert then import lib -- and the import was made deferred deliberately, because tests/test_restore_check.py runs that file as a single copied file with no bin/lib beside it and a module-scope import breaks it. THE DEFERRED IMPORT THEN FAILS AT EXACTLY THE MOMENT IT IS NEEDED. In that same lone-copy deployment -- the one the docstring at :184-191 names as the whole reason the function exists -- any --root raises ModuleNotFoundError, prints a traceback, and EXITS 1, which this tool's own contract defines as 'a path differs from the ref'. So a caller in the deployment the code was shaped around gets a false report of drift. Measured on all four vectors: --root <valid dir>, --root '', --root= and --allow-modified-self --root <dir>. --help and the no---root path still work, and the SHIPPED tool is correct -- only the lone copy is affected. NOTHING TESTS IT: _planted_copy and test_helper_outside_any_repository_refuses both run the lone copy and neither passes --root. GRADED ROW BY THE ROUND, NOT FAIL, and the reasoning is right: it fails closed and loudly, and spec 10b says a crash is not a silent wrong answer; the docstring's claim that the copy 'pays only if it is passed --root' is a comment defect, which review.md section 2 routes to a row. THE FIX IS SMALL: try/except ImportError falling back to the one-line rule, or move the empty check ahead of the import.
fields.title: perry-restore-check's deferred import fails in exactly the deployment its docstring says it exists for

fields.summary: FOUND BY V4 ROUND 8. DESIGN-016 goal 3 asks for 'an unknown argument refused with exit 2, with the legal set named, THE WAY perry-state --section ALREADY DOES IT'. The round checked that referent rather than assuming it: perry-state --section BOGUS exits 2 and lists all 22 keys, and the unknown-SUBCOMMAND path does the same. An unknown FLAG does not -- it says only 'unknown argument --wrte (try --help)'. So the tool is inconsistent with the exemplar its own goal names. THE ROUND ALSO SAID WHICH SHOULD MOVE AND I AGREE: the code, not the bar. The criteria file has been split into 3a (refused at exit 2, FAIL-grade) and 3b (names the legal set, ROW-grade), which is the same surgery already performed on criteria 2, 4, 10 and 14 and missed here. CONSEQUENCE IS SMALL AND REAL: the offender is named and the exit is right, so nothing writes and nothing lies -- a reader who wants the set types --help. It is filed because goal 3 asked for a specific thing, the tool does something narrower, and until now neither the code nor the document admitted the gap.
fields.title: an unknown flag does not name the legal set, while the exemplar goal 3 cites does

fields.summary: TWO FINDINGS FROM V4 ROUND 8, BOTH OUT OF THAT ROUND'S BOUNDS AND BOTH REAL. (1) perry-decide list --dry-run, perry-knowledge list --dry-run and perry-goals krs --dry-run all exit 0 with the flag swallowed. That is criterion 12's shape -- section 1.4, the accepted-and-dropped complaint this whole design was opened on -- but Bound G is 'the declared pairs in the six SURFACE blocks' and none of these three declares a SURFACE, so the round could not charge it. Consequence is low: all three subcommands are read-only, so a dropped --dry-run changes nothing. It is worth closing because the NEXT flag dropped by these parsers may not be read-only. (2) perry-config show cannot tell 'unreadable' from 'absent'. With .perry/config.jsonl present and .perry at mode 000 it prints 'this project declares nothing -- no .perry/config.jsonl, or an empty one.' at exit 0, BYTE-IDENTICAL to the answer for a directory with no .perry at all. The library already distinguishes them: viewer/parsers section config_store_records documents unreadable as one of its three reasons and returns it, and TASK-407's own test class docstring says so. The tool collapses a distinction its own reader hands it. Out of criterion 10's text -- this is an answer, not a refusal or a bad invocation -- which is why the round filed it rather than failing on it.
fields.title: three read-only subcommands accept --dry-run and drop it, and perry-config show cannot tell an unreadable config from an absent one

fields.summary: FOUND BY TASK-341's FIRST V4 ROUND, 2026-09-10, AND IT PREDATES THAT ROW. Adding 'templates' -- a directory holding 2 files in _domain() -- to SKIP_DIRS stops it being guarded, and in a git archive copy ALL 20 TESTS PASS. Two things have to line up for that: test_the_guard_domain_is_the_censuss_domain self-skips with 'not a git checkout', and shipped_dirs() applies THE SAME SKIP_DIRS, so the scratch tree never gets a templates/ directory and the plant test has nothing to plant into. THE ARCHIVE COPY IS NOT A CORNER CASE HERE -- it is how every reviewer on this board does destructive work, because review-constraints.md tells them to copy the project rather than mutate it in place. So the one environment where the guard is most likely to be exercised is the one where it cannot see this. NOT A REGRESSION FROM TASK-341: the round ran the identical mutation against 0724fa6c^1, the pre-fix tree, and it is equally green there -- the old code built its plant targets from the same SKIP_DIRS-filtered iterdir(). SUGGESTED FIX FROM THE ROUND: derive the plant set independently of SKIP_DIRS, or assert _domain()'s per-directory file counts against a live floor so a directory that empties out is reported rather than silently exempt.
fields.title: SKIP_DIRS narrows the guard's domain and builds the plant set, so a directory can stop being guarded with every test green

fields.summary: MEASURED TWICE ON 2026-09-10, ONCE BY A REVIEWER AND ONCE BY THE PMO. python3 -m unittest tests.<name> does NOT put tests/ on sys.path -- tests/parallel documents this at its own line 13 -- so a module importing a sibling helper fails to import and unittest reports Ran 1 test with a _FailedTest placeholder. THE FAILURE MODE IS THAT IT LOOKS FINE. TASK-341's reviewer built a poller to measure how long a probe file exists in the live tree, got 0 foreign files out of 1861 runs in 60 seconds, and only caught it because the run count was implausible: the module never imported, so the looper span at 30ms doing nothing. Its own words: a 0 from a poller is only worth the run count beside it. The PMO hit the same wall running tests.test_risks directly and saw ModuleNotFoundError: no module named task_writer_support. THE DANGEROUS CASE IS NOT THE ERROR, IT IS THE ZERO. An import error is loud when you are looking at it and silent when it is one number inside a measurement. THE FIX THE ROUND PROPOSED IS ONE LINE in a shared helper: refuse a module run that reports Ran 1 test from unittest.loader._FailedTest. It would have caught both instances.
fields.title: python3 -m unittest tests.<name> reports a clean pass for a module that never imported, and it has now cost two rounds

fields.summary: FOUND BY V4 ROUND 8 ATTACKING CRITERION 13 FROM A SIXTH DIRECTION, 2026-09-10. THREE LISTS: bin/perry-state section split_stages:301 treats only the em-dash as nothing; bin/lib/__init__.py:267 is_blank_cell accepts SIX spellings from schema section i18n.blank_cell; bin/perry-lint:354 UNDECLARED_CELL knows TEN. MEASURED CONSEQUENCE: a store record whose stages cell holds -, en-dash, n/a, N/A, none or 无 makes --compact report stage_list ['无'] with stages_declared true -- a stage named after the blank marker -- and perry-lint's suspect-separator guard skips exactly those cells, so nothing reports it. NOT REACHABLE THROUGH THE SHIPPED WRITER: perry-config track --stages normalises all three blanks to empty before they reach the store, which the round measured rather than assumed. So this needs a hand-edited store, and it is why the round filed it instead of failing the row. PRE-EXISTING: the code is byte-identical at 4ebc0693 and ec262f45. AND --json IS WRONG THE SAME WAY, which USER-924's reading 1 assigns to the producing function rather than to the projection -- so this row is where it lands. THIS IS THE N-IMPLEMENTATIONS-OF-ONE-RULE SHAPE, for the fourth time on this board: ADR-019's header_index, USER-906's shrink invariant, USER-915's render_row, and now the blank cell. Each previous one was closed by choosing a single symbol rather than a smarter detector.
fields.title: three tools carry three different lists of what a blank cell looks like, so a track's stages can be named after the blank marker

fields.summary: FOUND BY V4 ROUND 9, 2026-09-11. COMPACT:2256-2257 names NINE fields of project.tracks[]; the payload carries TWELVE. The one that matters is missing_defaults. schema section work_modes:64 says conflating 'there is no honest default, the track must declare it' with 'this mode has no such control' IS A BUG, in its own words -- and missing_defaults is the only field that separates them. A consumer reading only --compact cannot tell the two apart, and --compact is what SKILL.md step 3 mandates. GRADED ROW BY THE ROUND AND I AGREE: a narrowing announces itself by absence -- the key is not there, so nobody reads a wrong value from it -- which is a different harm from a value that is present and wrong. But --compact exists precisely so a standup need not read --json, so 'read --section project for that one' is a real answer only if the contract says it out loud.
fields.title: --compact drops missing_defaults from project.tracks[], the one field that separates 'no honest default' from 'this mode has no such control'

fields.summary: FOUND BY TASK-253's ROUND, 2026-09-11, AND IT IS THE ONLY SITE OF ITS KIND IN bin/. bin/perry-task:1061 hands the reader perry-migrate and perry-conform declare. USER-910 deleted perry-migrate along with perry_schema.py and test_migrate.py; perry-conform went with it. So a reader who follows the advice gets command not found. THAT IS STRICTLY WORSE THAN THE ROOTLESS HAND-BACKS THIS ROW WAS ABOUT: a rootless command runs and acts on the wrong project, which is bad; a command that does not exist cannot be followed at all, and the reader is left in the failure state the message was trying to get them out of. WHY THE ROUND FILED IT RATHER THAN FIXING IT, and I agree: choosing what to say instead is a PRODUCT decision. The two tools were deleted because ADR-019 and USER-910 decided migration was not Perry's job, so the honest replacement is not a different command -- it may be a sentence explaining that the situation no longer has a tool. That is not in TASK-253's scope and should not be invented by an agent mid-round. A CHEAP GUARD IS AVAILABLE REGARDLESS: a test that no message in bin/ names a tool absent from bin/, with the tool set DERIVED rather than listed. TASK-253's own guard already derives its population that way and found 126 command phrases doing it.
fields.title: bin/perry-task hands back perry-migrate and perry-conform declare, both deleted tools

fields.summary: intake has intake-sweep and asks does not, so every answered USER- row stays in BOARD.md forever. All 27 rows in the section are answered and 0 are pending; they are the single largest block of a board that is 30+ lines over its 200-line cap, and no tool path exists to remove them. The same one-way pressure modes/queue.md describes for intake applies here and was never implemented for asks.
fields.title: The User Input Queue has no sweep, so 27 answered asks cannot leave the board

fields.summary: MEASURED 2026-09-11 WHILE FIXING TASK-362, ON A WORKTREE OF 583f024f. bin/perry-task cmd_add writes values[track] only inside if mode != project, so a row filed with --track T against a PROJECT-mode track T is accepted, exits 0, and stores track main. Probed across all four modes: project stores main, pipeline/queue/inquiry store T. The consequence is not cosmetic and was found through it -- cmd_done reads track_of(config, values[track]), so the row closes at the IMPLICIT main track's Default rung instead of T's. Declaring T with Default rung V6 and closing a row raised with --track T stamps V3. THE COMMENT TWO LINES ABOVE THAT BRANCH REFUSES --stage FOR EXACTLY THIS REASON: 'Swallowing it is the same silent discard --commitment used to perform: the caller believes they set something.' --track is swallowed immediately below it. This is DESIGN-016 section 1.4's accepted-and-silently-dropped, the complaint that design was opened on, in the writer rather than the parser. The row must DECIDE which is right -- project mode may genuinely have one track, in which case --track on a project-mode track is a refusal and not a stored cell -- and then make the tests say so.
fields.title: perry-task add --track is accepted and dropped on a project-mode track

fields.summary: FOUND 2026-09-11, AND THE FIRST READING OF IT WAS WRONG -- read the whole entry, the correction is the point. WHAT STARTED IT: test_diagnose.TestUserLoadFindings.test_perry_itself_passes_its_own_id_checks went red on Perry's own project at 7f43a11c, reporting user_load.dangling == ['USER-920']. USER-920 is cited in TASK-281's Next action and has no row anywhere; neighbours 918, 919, 921 and 922 all have one, and git log -S finds no commit where 920 did. ISOLATED BY REMOVAL on scratch copies: replacing the journal's mention clears the finding, replacing only the .perry/events.jsonl mention does not. The journal line is what trips it. THE FIRST CONCLUSION, NOW REFUTED: that the project was PERMANENTLY dirty, because the journal is append-only and USER-920 can never be minted again (a probe filing a row produced USER-926). It is not permanent. Four hours later, same code, the finding was gone. Isolated again, one state file at a time: swapping in the day's journal ALONE clears it. Then the three obvious candidates were each excluded by probe -- deleting the second USER-920 mention from that journal leaves it green, deleting TASK-436's own row leaves it green, and the merges since 7f43a11c touch no code perry-diagnose runs. SO THE REAL DEFECT IS WORSE AND DIFFERENT: THE VERDICT MOVES WITH UNRELATED CONTENT ELSEWHERE IN THE JOURNAL. Same code, same dangling id, same citation, and the answer flips because other lines were written. A guard whose verdict changes when you write something unrelated is not a guard, and it cannot be used as a gate in either direction -- a green run proves nothing and a red one names the wrong cause. THE ROW MUST FIND WHAT ACTUALLY DECIDES IT, which this entry deliberately does not guess at, and then decide what a reference is: a journal is history, and an id cited in a record of what happened on a Tuesday is not a claim that the id exists now. If history stays in the domain, the check needs a remedy a project can perform.
fields.title: perry-diagnose reads the append-only journal as a live reference, so one mistyped id dirties a project forever

fields.summary: FOUND BY TASK-348's CENSUS AND VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY BY THE PMO, 2026-09-11, ON MAIN. bin/perry-goals line 963 calls lib.task_status_index(getattr(snap, 'project_root', '.'), ...). The task store lives under the STATE root. Two lines above, the same function correctly passes snap.state_root to load_linkage_store with the comment 'state_root, not project_root: the store sits beside the register' -- so the right value is in hand and the wrong one is used. MEASURED ON PERRY'S OWN PROJECT, where the two roots differ (project root is the repository, state root is perry/): task_status_index called with project_root returns 157 rows, called with state_root returns 430, and the store holds 430 records. perry-goals therefore computes every KR's progress over 37 percent of the work, falling back to the 157 rendered board rows because the store is not where it looked. THE ANSWER IS PLAUSIBLE AND NOBODY CAN TELL: it returns a number, not an error, and no test compares it against perry-state's. This is review.md section 0's second question -- a tool reporting a wrong answer to someone with no way to detect it. It is invisible on a project whose two roots coincide, which is why it survived.
fields.title: perry-goals computes KR progress from 157 of 430 task records, because it hands a project root where a state root is required

fields.summary: FOUND BY V4 ROUND 11 ON TASK-362 AND SHARPENED BY THE PMO'S INDEPENDENT CHECK, 2026-09-11. perry-config track --default-rung writes without validation and perry-task done stamps the cell verbatim. Measured on three values: Default rung 'banana' stores 'banana' and perry-lint reports 1 error; 'V9' stores 'V9' and lint reports 1 error; 'V0' stores 'V0' AND PERRY-LINT REPORTS 0 ERRORS. All three are refused at exit 1 when a caller passes the same value to done --rung. V0 is the one that matters and the reason is structural: V0 is IN schema enums.verification_rung, because a linter has to be able to name it, while check_rung refuses it by name as 'the label for what is being rejected, never a rung a row may carry'. So a closed row can carry V0 through the store, through the schema, and through the linter, and only the path a human types is guarded. THIS IS NOT CRITERION 13'S DEFECT and round 11 was right not to fail the row for it: the store holds what the payload publishes, so the equality criterion 13 asserts still holds. The defect is downstream and identical before and after round 10's fix. Round 11 filed it because it widens the bound rather than sitting inside it.

fields.question: TASK-050 has now failed SEVEN V4 rounds and needs a decision, not a round 8. Each round's fix moved the same defect rather than closing it: round 5's reviewer defeated a regex, round 6 replaced it with an AST walk, and round 7 showed the walk's gate is still an allowlist of variable names (ROW_NAMES, 11 entries). Measured: of 829 mapping constructs in the 18 readers, 59 are classified as row-cell sources and 35 of those are the bare name 'header'; FOUR LIVE header resolutions (viewer/parsers.py:1827, bin/perry-task:6029 and :6200, bin/perry-tasks:925) can be reverted to the exact historical defect with the whole 2793-test suite green, and parsers.py:1827 silently drops a KR when reverted. In the other direction the check now reports CORRECT code — 6 of 8 legitimate shapes flagged, including the exact latent risk round 5 recorded. Blind to four of the tree's own header resolutions AND loud about a keyword tokenizer: both failure modes the spec names, in one artefact. THE CHOICE. (A) Round 8, same shape — widen the source-expression recognition. The record says this is the fourth time that has moved the defect. (B) Invert the burden: flag EVERY case-folding map in a reader, and require the ~30 legitimate value normalizers to carry a one-line opt-out marker. Correct code declares itself once; anything new is caught by default. Cost: touching 30 live sites and a new convention. (C) RECOMMENDED — make it structurally impossible: one header_index() function becomes the only thing allowed to fold a header, and the guard becomes 'nothing outside it calls squash on a row', which is a one-symbol surface instead of a shape. This is the move ADR-007 already made for stores. (D) Accept the guard as advisory rather than a gate, close the row at a lower rung, and document the limitation. My recommendation is C, with B as the fallback. All four are design decisions with blast radius beyond this row, which is why this is an ask and not a dispatch. Evidence: evidence/2026-08/TASK-050-round7-v4-review.md.

fields.answer: 决定 2026-08-29（用户拍板，Perry 推荐 A + 回退）。两个决定。(1) 原则：选 A —— 一条表里声明、store 里被反驳的轨道就是 drift。处处适用：一张声明 queue/4/3d 的表配一个只记 project 的 store 必须 WARN，无论那条被反驳的轨道是 main 还是别的。理由：perry-lint 已经在算这条规则，而三轮的根因正是在写入侧反复重新推导它 —— 交给已经拥有它的那一方，不要第二份实现。第 5 轮 have 用名字集合比较必须改成按记录比较。(2) 拒绝宽度：回退到第 4 轮的窄宽度（source=store-default），立即恢复那三条被硬挡的普通手改流程。perry-config write --from-file 退出 1 的缺陷单独一行（已在 Intake），修好之前不再谈放宽。全部在未合并分支上，生产未受影响。
fields.question: TASK-095 has now failed FIVE V4 rounds and needs a decision, not a round 6. I caused three of the five, and every one is the same shape: two situations answered as one, one step to the left of the last. Round 1 collapsed four None-returns. Round 2 collapsed 'no-track-record' into unusable and hard-blocked three of this repo's own fixtures. Round 3 collapsed the two default cases. Round 4 filtered on the NAME 'main' instead of on whether the table DECLARED it. Round 5 compares on names over records, so a record that CONTRADICTS a declared row counts as carrying it. THE DECISION, and the reviewer states it cleanly: two principles are each defensible applied once, and round 5 applies one to the synthesised main and the other to the recorded main. (A) 'A declared row the register contradicts is drift' — then a table declaring queue/4/3d beside a store recording project must WARN, and perry-lint already computes exactly that. (B) 'The store is truth and the table is a stale projection' — then the trackless case must be SILENT too, because the register answered there as well. Pick one and it applies everywhere; the current code cannot be right because it holds both. SECOND, SEPARATE DECISION — the refusal WIDTH, and it is urgent because I made it worse: I widened the write refusal from source=store-default to source=store, and the reviewer measured three ordinary hand-edit workflows now hard-blocked that wrote at 45a355d AND at round 4. On the third — derive the store from a two-track table, then hand-swap one row — 'perry-config write --from-file', the ONLY command both refusal messages name, exits 1. The block cannot be cleared by the documented remedy. Options: revert to round 4's narrower width; make it a warning rather than a refusal; or fix perry-config so the remedy works. THIRD: the perry-goals half of the guard is a tautology — deleting it leaves the full 2875-test suite at exactly the baseline, which is the same defect TestTheGoalsLaneRefusesToo's own docstring records against round 2. My recommendation: (A) for the principle, because perry-lint already owns that rule and the root cause across three rounds has been re-deriving it differently; plus revert the refusal width to round 4's until perry-config's remedy is fixed. All of this is on an UNMERGED branch, so nothing is harmed in production. Evidence: evidence/2026-08/TASK-095-round5-v4-review.md.

fields.answer: 决定 2026-08-29（用户拍板，Perry 推荐 B）：选 B —— 一条不变量取代第四个谓词。普通写入永远不得缩小一个 canonical store：只有显式的移除命令（purge、resolve-intake、intake-sweep）可以减少记录数，任何会产出比 store 现有记录更少的推导都是 refusal 而不是写入。这一条覆盖三轮里找到的全部四扇门 —— 命令名、非唯一元组、四种 section 形状、ensure_section 的顺序 —— 而不是再加一个「门在什么时刻被读」的判断。不选 A：那是这一行上第四次「把问题挪一步」，前三次看上去也都有原则。不选 C/D：DoD Must-Have 2 明文点名 intake.jsonl 和 asks.jsonl，这条 Must-Have 保留，phase 003 不放弃它。同轮附带的三项一并修：第三个 shape 测试是空测（legend 落在 ## Top risks 之下，foreign 形状在任何 register 上都没有测试）；唯一性测试分不清唯一性与相邻；load_register_records 让 JSONDecodeError 以裸 traceback 逃逸，而该文件里其他每个失败都是 Refused。
fields.question: TASK-203 has now failed THREE V4 rounds, all three mine, and every one has ended with the same defect: an ordinary command silently truncates a canonical register store. I said I would escalate rather than attempt a fourth, so here it is. ROUND 3's FAIL: the gate is read at a moment the command controls. cmd_add's queue-mode branch calls ensure_section('Intake') BEFORE commit() asks the gate, so the gate sees a freshly created, readable, EMPTY table, answers yes, derives [] and writes zero bytes. Measured: a 291-byte 3-record intake.jsonl goes to 0 on 'perry-task add --track ops' with rc 0, byte-identical on 45a355d, and perry-lint reports '0 row(s) drifted'. It is round 1's blocking finding word for word — round 2 closed it for the project-mode track and never asked the queue-mode track, which is the mode ## Intake exists for. Three more doors of the same shape: intake 3->1, ask 3->1, risk-add 3->1, all rc 0, all preserved on base. THE DECISION. (A) Evaluate the gate against the board AS IT WAS AT COMMAND ENTRY, not after the command mutated it — snapshot the shape before any board write. Principled and small, but it is the fourth 'move the question' fix on this row and the first three all looked principled too. (B) RECOMMENDED — make it structurally impossible: an ordinary write may never SHRINK a canonical store. Only an explicit removal command (purge, resolve-intake, intake-sweep) may reduce the record count, and any derivation that would produce fewer records than the store holds is a refusal, not a write. That is one invariant covering every door found in three rounds — the command name, the non-unique tuple, the four section shapes, and the ensure_section ordering — instead of a fourth predicate. (C) Revert TASK-203 entirely and reconsider the row. It has introduced a store-truncation regression in all three rounds; before it, intake.jsonl did not exist and could not be wrong. That is a real 'should we do this at all' question and it deserves an answer, not an assumption. (D) Narrow the scope to the risks register only, which is the one that already existed, and defer intake/asks. NOTE THIS AFFECTS THE PHASE: TASK-203 is the ONLY row under P003-O1-KR1, and DoD Must-Have 2 names intake.jsonl and asks.jsonl explicitly, so (C) or (D) means the phase misses that Must-Have deliberately rather than by accident. Also filed from this round: my third shape test is VACUOUS (the legend table lands under ## Top risks because ensure_section anchors ## Intake before ## P0, so the foreign shape has no test on any register); the uniqueness test cannot distinguish uniqueness from adjacency; load_register_records lets a JSONDecodeError escape as an uncaught traceback where every other failure in that file is a Refused. Evidence: evidence/2026-08/TASK-203-round3-v4-review.md.

fields.answer: 决定 2026-08-29（用户拍板，Perry 推荐 a）：选 (a) 重述这条 KR。P003-O2-KR3 改成 ADR-010 能满足的东西 —— 「渲染能区分哪些是投影、哪些是 canonical」。理由：这条 KR 买的从来不是「文件里有标记」这个实现，而是「读者能分辨真相和投影」这个读者可见的属性，而那个需求在新表面上原样成立。TASK-199 因此重定范围而不是作废，phase 003 也不需要记录一条被撤回的 KR。写 KR 是 goals lane 的权，已在 handoff/2026-08-29-goals-lane-after-design-013.md 交接；这条 ask 是决定，不是那次写入。
fields.question: ADR-010 deletes BOARD.md, which makes P003-O2-KR3 unmeetable mid-phase — the KR is 'BOARD.md's two truth models are marked in the file' and TASK-199 is its only row. A boundary cannot be marked in a file that is gone. This needs your decision because dropping a KR changes what phase 003's Definition of Done MEANS, and the phase is live. THREE OPTIONS. (a) RESTATE the KR as something ADR-010 can satisfy — 'the render distinguishes what is projected from what is canonical' — which is the same reader-facing property the KR was actually buying, on a surface that will exist; TASK-199 is re-scoped rather than dropped. This is my recommendation: the KR was never really about the file, it was about a reader being able to tell truth from projection, and that need survives. (b) DROP the KR and TASK-199, recording that phase 003 closes with one KR withdrawn by a decision made DURING the phase. Honest, and it makes the phase score mean what it says. (c) Keep both and mark the boundary on a file scheduled for deletion — cheapest to do, hardest to defend. NOTE ON PROCESS: TASK-199 has been left not_started and untouched on purpose. Dropping the row is the visible half of dropping the KR, and doing the visible half first would make the record say the KR FAILED rather than that it was WITHDRAWN. The goals lane owns the edit either way; this ask is the decision, not the write. Full context: handoff/2026-08-29-goals-lane-after-design-013.md

fields.answer: 决定 2026-08-29（用户拍板，Perry 推荐 b 然后 c）：授权重写未推送的本地历史修复 0d68034，并加守卫。授权已给出。但执行顺序必须倒过来，理由是测量出来的，不是我改主意：重写 0d68034 会改掉它之后每一个 commit 的 SHA，包括 6c0d041 和 8abd30d —— 而那正是当前四个在飞分支的 merge base（coding/task-050-header-index、coding/task-203-round4、coding/task-095-round6 都在 6c0d041，coding/task-157-kr-declared-once 在 8abd30d），其中三个还在跑。现在重写会让它们的 merge base 消失，把已完成的工作推进一次不必要的 rebase，而这些行正是 phase 003 的 Must-Have。所以：(c) 现在做 —— 一行守卫，让下一次这类问题在合并时被机器抓住；(b) 在四个分支落地之后立刻做，那时 origin/main 仍然在 45a355d，未推送这个便宜窗口还开着。如果在那之前发生了 push，(b) 作废，答案永远变成 (a)：那条 hook 规则保护的是共享历史，一旦共享就不该动。
fields.question: May Perry rewrite unpushed local history to repair commit 0d68034? MEASURED 2026-08-29: at that commit, every perry-task write on a project carrying .perry/config.jsonl dies with AttributeError: module 'perry_state' has no attribute 'defaulted_over_a_declaring_table' — bin/perry-task at :6773 calls a function that arrives one commit later. The TASK-213 commit also carries the bin/perry-task half of TASK-095 round 4. Its own message's suite claim is FALSE at that commit. The branch tip was whole and main is whole; only this one commit does not build. It is now in main's history via the 777d021 merge, so a git bisect across the 20 commits after it gets a false 'broken' verdict there. WHY THIS IS AN ASK: .perry/hook.md lists git history rewrites — push --force, --force-with-lease, rebase onto main, tag deletion — as high-stakes operations requiring your explicit authorization. I filed it rather than doing it, and a V4 reviewer endorsed that: 'That reasoning is correct and I endorse it — do not rewrite.' WHAT CHANGED SINCE: origin/main is at 45a355d and local main is at 91e5351, so all 27 commits including this one are UNPUSHED. Nobody has seen this history. That materially lowers the risk the hook rule is written for — the rule protects shared history, and this is not shared yet. OPTIONS. (a) LEAVE IT, and document the bad commit so a future bisect knows to skip it. Zero risk, permanent small cost, and the record keeps an honest scar. (b) REWRITE the unpushed history to move the perry-task hunk into the commit that owns it, then verify every commit in the range builds. My recommendation IF you want a clean history, because unpushed is the only moment this is cheap — after a push it becomes a shared-history rewrite and the answer should be (a) forever. (c) Leave the history and add a test that every commit on main builds standalone, so this class is caught at the next merge rather than by a person. Slower, and it does not fix this commit. My recommendation is (b) THEN (c) — repair it while it is still free, and add the guard so the next one is caught by a machine. But this is your call and I will not touch history without it.

fields.answer: (a), scoped to a high-water mark. perry-decide appends a mint event to .perry/events.jsonl and mint_id takes max(files union events), so an id once issued is never reissued -- the same rule as perry-task's minting_records. Three measurements on d49964e reshaped the choice and belong to the implementing row. (1) Only the HIGHEST id reissues; a middle gap is never filled -- delete ADR-002 of five and the next mint is ADR-006 -- so what is needed is a durable high-water mark, not an event surface on every command. (2) Option (b) "refuse the delete" was rejected because perry-decide has no delete command to refuse: bootstrap/new/supersede/status/list only, and an ADR leaves decisions/ by a human rm, so (b) could only ever be documentation plus a lint detector, never enforcement. (3) The cheap counter-file fix is foreclosed by TASK-235's own guard, tests/test_decide_writer.py:461 ADR_ONLY = ^decisions/ADR-\d+-[^/]+\.md$, which permits nothing but ADR bodies in decisions/. The remaining durable home is .perry/events.jsonl, whose schema owner is "perry" rather than a lane, so decide writing there does not breach the hand-off contract. Current exposure: ADR-012 is the top id (8 citations); ADR-007 (321) and ADR-004 (237) are reachable only after every id above them is deleted first.
fields.question: perry-decide REISSUES a retired ADR id, and perry-task does not — two tools, one contract, opposite answers. Measured by the TASK-235 agent 2026-08-29: delete ADR-011's file and the next mint hands out 011 again. perry-task purge retires an id through the append-only event log so it is never reissued; perry-decide writes NO events at all, so it has nothing to retire an id with. Worse, before TASK-235 the behaviour was NON-DETERMINISTIC: on main an unrelated write re-rendered the index and the next mint reissued anyway. THE STAKE: an ADR id is an address. ADR-007 is cited by name in ADR-010, in DESIGN-013, in three task rows and in this project's own commit messages. If 011 can name two different decisions, every one of those citations becomes ambiguous the moment an ADR is deleted and a new one minted. This did not matter while nobody deleted ADRs; TASK-235 is the row that made deletion ordinary. THE OPTIONS. (a) RECOMMENDED — perry-decide writes events like every other writer, and an id is retired the way perry-task retires one. This is the answer that makes the two tools agree rather than documenting why they differ, and DESIGN-004's whole posture is that every write goes through a tool and leaves a trace. Cost: perry-decide gains an event surface it does not have today. (b) Refuse the delete instead: an ADR file may not be removed, only superseded — which is arguably what a decision record SHOULD mean, since ADR-005 and ADR-007 are cited as history and history is not deleted. Cheaper, and it may be more correct in principle. (c) Accept reissue, and document that an ADR id is a slot rather than an address. Honest but it silently breaks every existing citation. (d) Leave it declared as it is now — the TASK-235 agent pinned the disagreement with a named test rather than resolving it silently, so nothing is hidden and the row can close. My recommendation is (b) THEN (a): stop the deletion that creates the problem, then give perry-decide the event surface so the two tools stop disagreeing on principle rather than by accident. But (b) changes what a decision record IS, which is yours and not mine.
