fields.answer: WITHDRAW P003-O2-KR2, with the reason recorded. Decided 2026-09-02 after the ask's own four options were measured and three of them collapsed. THE PREMISE WAS WRONG, and this is the finding rather than the decision: the KR asks for "the adoption reader fenced into ONE NAMED MODULE", and that module does not exist and never did. Measured on 185c208: viewer/parsers.py is 4,606 lines and EIGHT tools import it -- perry-task, perry-lint, perry-goals, perry-decide, perry-diagnose, perry-knowledge, perry_store.py, perry_md_store.py. It carries no adopt- or migrate-specific top-level definition at all; its mentions of adoption are READ SEMANTICS ("there is legitimately no store, this is the adoption path", "a project with NO store has not been adopted, its markdown IS its state"), not a separable half. The re-baseline of 2026-09-01 was right that the file serves ONE role -- but that role is Perry's shared reader, not adoption. Two further corrections to what the ask asserted. (1) /perry adopt is NOT unimplemented: reference/adoption.md is 26,944 bytes, SKILL.md:27 routes it, and first-run step 4 sends an existing project to it. What was deleted was perry-migrate, and adoption.md already says so in the past tense at line 441. (2) /perry adopt does not go through parsers.py at all -- the agent reads README, CHANGELOG, docs/ and git history directly, so the reader's callers are the eight tools above and not adoption. THEREFORE: (a) "fence it anyway" has nothing to fence; (b) "delete the adoption half" would delete the shared read layer eight binaries stand on; (c) "fence what the store readers touch" describes a real boundary -- tolerant parsing versus strict store reading, 25 tolerance sites inside one file -- but eight callers straddle it and the work is far larger than the KR ever contemplated, on phase day 6. The KR describes a structure that does not exist, so it is a KR that cannot be met rather than work that was not done. Phase 003 scores on 6 KRs, not 7, and the record must show WITHDRAWN and not FAILED. THE WRITE IS THE GOALS LANE'S: phase/003-linkage.md and phase/003-storage-code.md are goals-owned, perry-goals krs is READ-ONLY and is the only surface for KRs, so there is no tool path -- that gap is TASK-264. TASK-099 is freed by this and needs re-scoping: its fence half is withdrawn with the KR, and whether its sweep half still earns a row is now an open question rather than a blocked one.
fields.question: Should the adoption reader be fenced at all, now that it has no caller? P003-O2-KR2's metric asks for 'the adoption reader fenced into one named module, with a mechanical guard shown able to go red'. Its own re-baseline of 2026-09-01 then removed the ground under it: bin/perry-migrate was DELETED 2026-08-31 by TASK-261, TASK-097 was dropped with it, and /perry adopt is a user-facing command whose implementation went too. So viewer/parsers.py's 4,603 lines now serve ONE role, and the KR text says in its own words that 'whether an unreachable reader is still worth fencing is the open question TASK-099 carries into the pivot rather than an assumption this KR may keep making'. The phase file lists this under User Commitments as 'a product decision rather than a review'. THE OPTIONS. (a) FENCE IT ANYWAY -- a boundary that exists before the caller returns is cheaper than one retrofitted after, and /perry adopt is a documented command someone will re-implement. Cost: a guard around code nothing calls, which is also a guard nothing exercises, and an unexercised guard is the class of check this project keeps finding rotten. (b) DO NOT FENCE; delete the adoption half instead, on the ground that ADR-011 already condemns viewer/parsers.py as the representation layer and a reader with no caller is dead code by definition. Cost: /perry adopt cannot be re-implemented without restoring it, and the deletion is not this phase's declared scope. (c) FENCE ONLY WHAT THE STORE READERS TOUCH -- draw the boundary from the live side rather than the dead side, so the guard is exercised by code that actually runs. My recommendation, because it is the only one of the three whose guard can be shown able to go red by a test of live behaviour. (d) DEFER the whole KR to phase 004 and score P003-O2-KR2 as withdrawn, since its premise was deleted mid-phase. NOTE ON SEQUENCING: the SWEEP half of TASK-099 -- censusing bin/, viewer/ and tests/ for document handling ADR-007 made dead -- does NOT depend on this answer and is being dispatched separately, so the census will be on the table when you answer

fields.question: Recording the P003-O2-KR2 withdrawal is blocked by two walls, and both need your call because both are deliberate design constraints rather than bugs. THE DECISION IS ALREADY MADE (USER-911, answered 2026-09-02, withdraw the KR because its metric describes a module that does not exist). What is blocked is WRITING IT DOWN. WALL 1 -- the phase document is FULL. phase/003-storage-code.md is 300 lines against a cap of 300 declared cap_kind: hard in schema/state-schema.json, and tier-1 hard caps are one of only three hard blocks in Perry. goals/reference/pivots.md step 3 requires a '## Changes' line in that file with the old text left as strikethrough; there is no room for one. The tier-1 rule's own answer is to force overflow into a sibling appendix, leaving the main file a section index plus one-paragraph summaries -- but that is an editorial restructuring of a live phase document, mid-phase, and it is yours to authorise rather than mine to perform. WALL 2 -- the register has no write path and forbids hand edits. The phase KRs live in phase/<NNN>-linkage.md; perry-goals krs is READ-ONLY and calls itself 'the only surface for them'; goals/reference/phases.md:212 says 'nothing in this file is edited by hand once it exists'. The precedent cuts both ways: P003-O3-KR1 was withdrawn 2026-08-31 and its record is simply gone from the register today, so it was either a hand edit against that rule or an unwritten path. Recorded on TASK-264, which is the missing KR writer. THE OPTIONS. (a) COMPACT the phase document first -- move superseded strikethrough passages and older Changes entries into evidence/2026-09/phase-003-appendix.md, which the pre-pivot state already preserves in two snapshots taken today, then write the pivot entry normally. My recommendation: it obeys the cap rule as written and the history is already safe. (b) WRITE THE PIVOT ENTRY ANYWAY and let the document go to 301+, accepting a hard-cap breach that perry-lint will report at every snapshot. Honest and visible, but it makes the one cap the project treats as unbreakable breakable by convenience. (c) RECORD THE WITHDRAWAL ONLY IN THE REGISTER and skip the phase document entry, accepting that the phase's own narrative will not say why it scores on 6 KRs. Cheapest and worst -- the strikethrough plus reason is the whole point of pivots.md's friction. (d) DEFER the write until the phase closes and let score-phase record the withdrawal, leaving the KR live-but-known-dead in the meantime. NOTE: whichever you pick, step 4 of pivots.md hands off to the decide lane for an ADR recording the pivot rationale, and that half is unblocked

fields.answer: 决定 2026-09-03（用户拍板，Perry 推荐 a）：选 (a) —— 白名单。规则块逐字比对，四个规范性区域按 sha256 钉死；任何增删改写都变红，包括没人预料到的那种。理由散文故意不钉：观察记录和本地 merge 的论证可以继续改进而不动测试，不能悄悄变的是 agent 被要求做什么。代价接受：以后改这条规则必须在同一个提交里重新钉一次摘要，这个摩擦是有意的。不选 (b) 再拓宽黑名单 —— 那已经输了两次，第三次也只是猜下一个没被列进去的词。已实现，13 个突变 13 红。声明的限制保留在记录里：白名单只能钉住已存在的规范性文字，日后有人在它读不到的文件里新加第五处，它看不见。
fields.question: TASK-285 has FAILed two V4 rounds and perry-lint says another round is not the next step. UNUSUALLY, THE PRINCIPLE HAS ALREADY BEEN NAMED -- by the round 2 reviewer, not by me -- and I have already implemented it. This ask exists to have you confirm or overrule that, because a PMO who has just fixed something is the worst judge of whether the principle is settled. WHAT HAPPENED. The row writes one rule into three shipped files: a dispatched agent works in its own git worktree, the primary checkout is never switched by an agent and merges the branch afterwards. Round 1 defeated the guard by softening the rule to 'MAY ... where convenient' -- every assertion pinned the presence of words, none pinned modality. I fixed that with a denylist of eight hedge words. Round 2 then kept the pinned imperative VERBATIM, used none of the eight, and added one sentence inside the rule's own blockquote: 'Where a worktree is impractical, sharing the primary checkout instead is an acceptable alternative.' All nine tests reported OK with the headline deliverable retracted. It also walked past the push check with two synonyms (publishes / raises a pull request). Its summary: A DENYLIST OVER ENGLISH HAS NOW LOST THIS ARGUMENT TWICE. THE OPTIONS. (a) IMPLEMENTED AND MY RECOMMENDATION -- an allowlist. The rule block is compared literally and four normative regions are pinned by sha256; any addition, removal or rewording reddens. Rationale prose is deliberately NOT pinned, so the observed-failure account and the local-merge argument can still be improved without touching a test; what an agent is TOLD TO DO cannot change silently. Thirteen mutations, thirteen red, including both that defeated the old design and a single extra space. Cost: changing the rule now requires re-pinning a digest in the same commit, which is friction on purpose. This is the same move you chose in USER-904 (one header_index over a smarter detector) and USER-906 (one invariant over a fourth predicate). (b) Keep a denylist and widen it again. The record says this is the third widening and the first two each looked principled. (c) Accept the guard as advisory, close at a lower rung, document the limit. (d) Drop the guard entirely and rely on the fact that the rule is now in three files a reader sees. STATED LIMIT OF (a), because it is real: an allowlist pins what EXISTS and cannot cover a fifth normative region someone adds later in a file it does not read. Evidence: evidence/2026-09/TASK-285-round2-v4-review.md and TASK-285-result.md.

fields.answer: 决定 2026-09-03（用户拍板，Perry 推荐乙/B）：选 (B) —— 一个收口点。除 render_row 外没有东西构造表格行，守卫变成一个符号的检查面。这是本项目第三次选这个形状（USER-904 的 header_index、USER-906 的 shrink 不变量）。THE THIRD OPTION WAS OFFERED AND NOT TAKEN: 我另外提过「(B) 收口 + 把甲那 9 处里真正会写坏数据的 8 处也做掉」，用户选的是 (B) 本身，所以那 8 处不在这次范围内。因此实现时必须明确以下三点，它们是 (B) 买到的和没买到的，普查已经量过：(1) 7 个分隔行构造点只有在分隔行也被路由进收口点时才被覆盖 —— 今天没有，所以路由分隔行是 (B) 的一部分而不是附加项；(2) bin/perry-decide:332 不构造行，(B) 够不着它，它仍然开着；(3) bin/perry-task:7431 两种读法都不覆盖，是消息质量缺陷不是损坏路径。最重要的一条，按 Perry 的推荐记录：不要把 ragged-row 当成 (B) 的卖点。普查测出它在 w4-w7 有效、在 r2/r3/r4/r7/r8 不存在，读取侧有四个已证实盲点（maxsplit、re.split、SEP 常量、.rsplit/.partition），而且只在 schema 认得的表格里触发 —— round 1 用对照确认，同样的 8 格行放在不被识别的 section 里报 0 错误，所以用 add --group 的项目上这张网根本不存在。这些洞要写成声明的限制，不能让下一轮以为有兜底。
fields.question: TASK-067 has FAILed two V4 rounds and needs a principle chosen, not a third round. THE CENSUS THAT MAKES THIS ANSWERABLE NOW EXISTS: TASK-323 delivered a bound and a census and PASSED V4 round 2 on 2026-09-03, so unlike the last two rounds this choice is against measured numbers rather than a recollection. Both failed rounds carried criteria-unbounded because the criteria file had no bound; it now has one -- 89 members (27 W1 / 18 W2 / 38 R1 / 6 R2), last element viewer/tables.py:280, generated by a runnable script at evidence/2026-09/TASK-323-bound.py. Census: 20 rows, 12 caught, 8 uncaught, plus 13 shape rows with 4 red controls. THE TWO READINGS, with what each would actually have to cover. (A) EVERY WRITE PATH MUST REFUSE AN UNRENDERABLE CELL. Population is all writers. To close it must cover all 27 W1 members, already refusing, PLUS the 7 uncaught separator-row builders -- perry-task:985, :1034, :1112, :5174, perry_md_store.py:774, perry-goals:327-328, perry-goals:3093 -- PLUS bin/perry-decide:332, which guards with a weaker third spelling that misses a trailing newline, PLUS perry-task:7431. It would NOT cover the five uncaught read shapes, which are not writes. Its cost is visible in the bound itself: the population has no last element other than the current line count, which is exactly why this file had no bound for two rounds and why each round found a member the previous one never reached. (B) ONE CHOKE POINT PLUS ONE DETECTOR, MY RECOMMENDATION. To close it must cover ONE SYMBOL -- nothing outside render_row builds a row -- with ragged-row as the backstop. The census says precisely what that buys and what it does not: it covers the 7 separator builders by construction IF separator rows are routed through the choke point too, which they are not today; its backstop is MEASURED to work on w4-w7 and MEASURED not to exist for r2/r3/r4/r7/r8; ragged-row cannot cover the read side at all and .split('|', 6) proves no count-based check ever will; its detector has four demonstrated blind spots on the read half because SPLIT_RE matches none of maxsplit, re.split, a SEP constant, or .rsplit/.partition; and it does not reach perry-decide:332, which builds no rows. TWO MORE FACTS THE ROUNDS DID NOT HAVE. First, ragged-row fires ONLY inside a table the schema recognises -- round 1 confirmed with a control that the identical 8-cell row is silent in an unrecognised section -- so on a project filing work under its own headings via add --group, which Perry explicitly supports, (B)'s backstop does not exist. Second, both readings leave perry-task:7431 open; it is a message-quality defect rather than a corruption path. PRECEDENT, OFFERED AS PRECEDENT AND NOT AS AN ARGUMENT: you chose shape (B) in USER-904 after seven rounds and USER-906 after three. The census neither confirms nor contradicts that -- (B)'s one-symbol surface is real and measured, and so is the fact that its detector is green on nine shapes, five of which have no backstop of any kind. Evidence: evidence/2026-08/TASK-067-finding.md sections Bound, Census and The two readings; evidence/2026-09/TASK-323-round2-v4-review.md.

fields.answer: 答复 2026-09-04（用户拍板）：去掉。'bin/perry-state --escalation-scan 这个命令有问题啊，之前我们已经讨论过，不要用python代码来检查文件语义。应该去掉这个检查逻辑，让agent自己来判断gate。' 这是 ADR-007 决策 3 直接适用到派发闸门上：Python 层根本不解析文档，判断交给 agent。它推翻了 Perry 建议的另一条路 —— TASK-333 提的'把闸门输入换成类型化字段'不再是方向，因为那仍然是 Python 在读 spec，只是读得更窄。PERRY 量过的删除面（2026-09-04, main 7f890f9）：viewer/parsers.py 的 scan_spec_escalations 是 152 行，加上 _PATH_CHAR / _NAME_EDGE / escalation_occurrences / matching_escalations 这一串；调用点在 bin/perry-state（11 处）、bin/perry-lint（4 处）、work/reference/dispatch.md 和 autopilot.md 各 1 处；测试 tests/test_escalation_boundaries.py 1120 行 + test_escalation_union.py 719 行 + test_spec_scannability.py 里 7 处。ONE BOUNDARY THE DECISION DOES NOT SETTLE, and Perry is flagging it rather than assuming: 扫描 spec 的那一半明确要删，但 escalation_union / hook_escalation_lines 是从 .perry/hook.md 里抽出'什么算高风险'这份清单 —— agent 自己判断时仍然需要这份清单，只是它可以直接读那份文档。这一半是跟着删、还是留着当数据源，是实现行要回答的第一个问题。THE REAL RISK, stated plainly: 闸门武装着这个项目的每一次派发。删掉检查而不同时写下 agent 要遵循的判断程序，等于把闸门换成真空。所以实现行的交付物必须包含 work/reference/dispatch.md 里一段可执行的人写程序，而不只是删代码。WHAT THIS RETIRES: TASK-290（修 cite-vs-write）、TASK-329（markdown 斜体那个洞）、TASK-333（类型化字段）全部被这条取代；TASK-306 早已 dropped。TASK-099 由此解封 —— 它卡的就是 setup 这个词的误报。

fields.answer: 决定 2026-09-08：选 A —— 新增 --compact payload，从完整 payload 在进程内派生。--json 保持已发布的形状不变，所以 aiMark 和任何现有消费者不受影响，而窄模式可以作为一个严格投影来测试。重新测量后这个决定比立项时更紧迫：payload 从 09-04 的 186,856 bytes 涨到今天的 258,989 bytes（约 65k tokens），+39%，其中 board 一个 section 占 159,648 bytes = 72%。涨的是本会话加的十几行 task。第一手证据：今天开场跑 perry-state --json 输出 248.8KB 被系统直接转存到文件，因为塞不进上下文，此后整个会话都在从那个文件里抠字段。选项 C（只改 SKILL.md 用 --section）明确排除：board 单独就是 72%，达不到目标。
fields.question: DESIGN-016 Decision 1 — how the standup gets a small structured read. MEASURED 2026-09-04 on 5d19d83: SKILL.md:130 mandates perry-state --json every invocation and that payload is 186,856 bytes (~47k tokens) on this repository; its largest section, board, is 122,828 on its own; the only compact answer, --dashboard, is 1,132 bytes and text-only. perry-context-budget reports 99.1% of this project's 8.43B tokens is context re-read per turn, so this is the expensive kind of cost. A: add a --compact payload derived in-process from the full one and point SKILL.md step 3 at it (recommended — --json keeps its published shape, and the narrow mode can be tested as a strict projection). B: add --fields selection instead, so the caller names what it wants (more flexible, but every caller now has to know the field names). C: change nothing in the tool and narrow SKILL.md to a list of --section calls (cheapest, but board alone is still 31k tokens, so it does not reach the goal).

fields.answer: 决定 2026-09-08：选 B —— 论证搬进 bin/README.md，--help 只留 Usage 和子命令。重新测量：perry-task --help 169 行 10,690 字节，Usage 在第 51 行；perry-goals 107 行，Usage 在第 58 行；perry-decide 62 行，Usage 在第 41 行。而 perry-lint 同样长（136 行）Usage 却在第 8 行，说明这不是论证太多，是排版顺序。PMO 提出的风险，用户已知并接受：论证离开它解释的代码之后两边会各自漂移，而那正是 ADR-019 今天删掉的那一类重复。缓解办法应与搬迁同批交付，不是后补：bin/README.md 目前覆盖 19 个工具中的 19 个，但没有任何测试引用它，覆盖是手工维持的。搬迁应带一个机械检查——每个 bin/ 工具在 README 里有对应小节，且其 Usage 块与工具实际的 --help 一致——把漂移从静默变成被报告，这是 perry-lint 对其它投影已经在用的模式。
fields.question: DESIGN-016 Decision 2 — where the --help rationale goes. MEASURED 2026-09-04: perry-task answers --help with 160 lines / 10,059 bytes and its Usage block starts at line 51; perry-lint 135 lines, perry-goals 106, and four more tools put Usage past line 36. The prose above the fold is ADR numbers, the bug that motivated the tool and why each refusal is a refusal — it is good content and it is not what a caller asking for a flag list wants first. A: usage-first --help, rationale behind --help --verbose (recommended — nothing is lost and the default call gets cheap). B: move the rationale into bin/README.md and leave only usage in the tool (README is already 20KB and would grow). C: leave as-is and accept the ~2.5k token discovery cost per tool.

fields.answer: APPROVED 2026-09-08. Both additive edits made inline and verified with a three-armed differential: new grammar against the OLD schema draws 38 bad-id findings, against the NEW schema draws 0, and the OLD grammar against the new schema also draws 0 -- so nothing on the board or in the corpus breaks, which is what additive was supposed to mean. schema:1303 id_pattern is now ^(?:KR-O\d+\.\d+|O\d+-KR\d+)$ and the invariant list at 286 names O<n>-KR<m> alongside KR-O1.2. fields.question: ADR-017 step 1 is blocked on two ADDITIVE edits to schema/state-schema.json, which .perry/hook.md names as the claim surface and therefore yours. Line 1303 is id_pattern ^KR-O\d+\.\d+$ on the OKR table's Id column, enforced per row at bin/perry-lint:1203, and it is the definition of an overall KR id; it would become ^(?:KR-O\d+\.\d+|O\d+-KR\d+)$. NEITHER REMOVES THE OLD FORM, so nothing on the board or in the corpus breaks the moment they land -- they only stop the linter refusing the new grammar. The round declined to widen the parsers without this on a substantive ground worth your attention: 1303 IS the definition, so widening the parsers while it stands would leave Perry's parsers accepting an id Perry's own linter calls an error, which is the two-readers-one-grammar defect ADR-017 exists to close. Approving unblocks step 1; the data rename and the 74 test occurrences follow it.

fields.answer: (A) — give add a writer for the declaration. Chosen 2026-09-08. The KR keeps the distinction it exists to measure: never-asked and declared-no-KR stay two readings, which is what DESIGN-015 section 5.2 built the derivation to tell apart, and 100 percent becomes reachable rather than being redefined into reach. Filed as TASK-394 and dispatched.
fields.question: FOUND AND VERIFIED 2026-09-08 BY TASK-281 ROUND 2, AND CONFIRMED BY THE PMO ON THE MERGED TREE. bin/lib/__init__.py:741 computes half the P003-O3-KR2 numerator from records matching kind unlinked AND via add. NO WRITER ANYWHERE PRODUCES THAT SHAPE. via:add is hardcoded at exactly one site, bin/perry-task:2798, which writes EDGE records; bin/perry-goals:2022 appends an unlinked record carrying NO via field at all, and it is the goals lane, whose declarations are via link by definition. THE CONSEQUENCE IS ON THE PHASE, NOT ON A TOOL. Definition of Done item 5, as restated 2026-08-31, reads: every main-track row opened after the gate lands carries A KR EDGE OR AN UNLINKED DECLARATION WRITTEN BY ITS OWN add. The second half has no implementation, so a row that genuinely serves no KR CANNOT satisfy item 5 the way item 5 describes it. Its only available action is to omit --kr, which the computation counts as not-answered and puts in the denominator. SO EVERY HONEST no-KR ROW PERMANENTLY LOWERS THIS KR, and the 100 percent target is unreachable by construction rather than by not having done the work yet. THIS IS WHY THE NUMBER LOOKS THE WAY IT DOES. P003-O3-KR2 read 50 percent, then 33, then 15.38, and none of those moves was a regression -- the denominator grew as rows were filed and most of them legitimately serve no KR. The KR is measuring honestly and the target it is measured against cannot be reached. TWO RESOLUTIONS AND THEY ARE NOT EQUIVALENT. (A) GIVE add A WRITER for the declaration: a row can say at add time that it serves no KR, producing kind unlinked with via add, and it then counts as ANSWERED. This is what DoD item 5 already describes and it makes the 100 percent target reachable. (B) RESTATE THE KR so that omitting --kr counts as answered-with-none. Cheaper, but it destroys the distinction the KR exists to measure -- never-asked and declared-no-KR become the same reading, which is exactly the state DESIGN-015 section 5.2 built the derivation to tell apart. THE PMO RECOMMENDS (A), and the reason is that (B) makes the number un-interpretable rather than merely lower: after (B) a KR at 100 percent would tell you nothing about whether anybody was ever asked. This is a phase-scoring decision and phase/003-storage-code.md lists phase-scoring participation as a User Commitment, which is why it is an ask rather than a row the PMO takes.

fields.answer: SUPERSEDED BY USER-923, and this answer is bookkeeping rather than the user's decision on the substance. The option set here was incomplete: it listed keep / redraw-by-object / defer and omitted the fourth, which the PMO recommends and which the user asked to have written in. An ask cannot be re-worded once filed -- retitle and purge both refuse a row in the User Input Queue -- so it is superseded instead. USER-923 carries all four options and the two facts that changed the premise. Nothing about the boundary is decided by this.
fields.question: Is the bin/ tool boundary drawn on the mechanism or on the object? DESIGN-016 section 8 asks it, section 1.4 is the evidence, and Decision 3 explicitly did not rule on it. Four registers -- tasks, risks, intake, asks -- are each named twice, once by perry-task for their lane verbs and once by perry-tasks for their store verbs, in two tools that differ by one letter and disagree about singular/plural and about which side the verb goes on. Option A: keep the mechanism split as it is, and TASK-066's per-subcommand-group split of perry-task proceeds. Option B: redraw by object, one tool per register holding both its lane and store verbs, which makes TASK-066's split the wrong cut. Option C: neither now -- record the axis as decided-to-defer with a date, so it stops blocking. THIS IS A BREAKING CHANGE TO EVERY CALL SITE in the skill and in every project already using Perry, which is why DESIGN-016 section 1.4 calls itself a finding and not a proposal, and why it is the user's call rather than a task. NOT COSTED ANYWHERE YET: no one has measured how many call sites a rename touches.

fields.answer: OPTION B, AND ALL THREE PAIRS. Decided by the user 2026-09-10. The reason given is architectural rather than economic: two commands that differ by one character cannot coexist, and the cost of many external references is acceptable BECAUSE AGENTS DO THE WORK -- which is the premise that makes B affordable now and did not hold when section 1.4 was written. Scope is all three pairs section 1.4 names, not just the acute one: perry-task/perry-tasks differ by 1 character, perry-state/perry-state-cost by 5, perry-goals/perry-okr are the same shape with a different word. Renaming in three passes would break downstream projects three times and each later pass would be harder to justify than the first. WHAT B MEANS CONCRETELY: the boundary is redrawn on the OBJECT. perry-task keeps tasks alone; perry-risk, perry-intake and perry-ask appear, each holding both its everyday verbs and its store verbs; perry-tasks disappears and the confusable pair goes with it. THE PMO'S RESERVATION, RECORDED AND OVERRULED: under B a destructive maintenance verb sits beside an everyday one -- perry-risk render --write next to perry-risk add -- and render --write is the one command in this repository found reporting a write it had not performed. The user's answer is that the near-identical names are themselves the worse hazard. That is a decision to carry into the new design as a constraint on how the verbs are grouped, not a reason to revisit the axis. This does not go into DESIGN-016. That document is locked and decide/SKILL.md says a structural pivot needs a new doc; the redraw gets DESIGN-018 and DESIGN-016 section 9 records that its open question was answered there.
fields.question: Is the bin/ tool boundary drawn on the mechanism or on the object? Supersedes USER-922, which listed three options and was missing the one the PMO recommends. THE PROBLEM, in one sentence: there are two tools one letter apart -- perry-task writes rows the way you work every day, perry-tasks rebuilds and compares the stores behind them -- and to pick one you must know which KIND of operation you want before you can say WHICH THING you want it done to. The four things are tasks, risks, intake and asks. OPTION A -- leave it. TASK-066's per-subcommand-group split of perry-task then proceeds. OPTION B -- one tool per thing: perry-risk holds both its everyday verbs and its repair verbs. This is what DESIGN-016 section 8 asks. Costs 475 live call sites plus 623 in bin/, 200 in tests, 56 in viewer/, and every project already using Perry; the 4589 mentions in journal and evidence are history and must not be touched. OPTION C -- decide to defer, with a date, so it stops blocking TASK-066. OPTION D, RECOMMENDED BY THE PMO -- keep the two tools and let BOTH take the thing as a parameter. C5 already did this on the repair side: risks-build became perry-tasks build --register risks, with the register list read from schema section claims and the twelve old names kept as aliases for one release. The everyday side still spells the thing into the verb -- risk-add, intake-sweep, ask, answer -- eight subcommands. Finishing the same move there makes both tools symmetric and costs eight subcommands plus aliases instead of a rename. TWO FACTS THAT CHANGED THE PREMISE SINCE SECTION 1.4 WAS WRITTEN: (1) C5 already answered half the question in the object direction, so the prefix table is asymmetric because the work is half done, not because the design is confused; (2) section 1.4's complaint was that the names do not carry the distinction, and perry list and perry describe now carry it, so nobody has to read it out of a name. THE ARGUMENT FOR KEEPING THE MECHANISM SPLIT: the everyday side takes a lock, stamps an event, writes the journal and the board; the repair side does one-way imports and byte comparisons. Different risk classes. Under option B, perry-risk render --write sits one tab-completion from perry-risk add -- and render --write is the one place in this repository that was found reporting a write it had not performed.

fields.answer: READING 1. Decided by the user 2026-09-10. A projection is checked for whether it is applied CONSISTENTLY over its whole declaration; whether the value underneath is right belongs to the function that produces it, not to the projection of it. TASK-362 closes when every declared pair is compared from the KEY side: the ten subdict inner triples at bin/perry-state:2280-2289, the eleven arg-tuple names, and _at itself, which the tool and the test's expectation share. Bounded, finite, and round 7 specified the fix. THE FACT THAT DECIDES IT, measured rather than argued: --json is ALREADY pinned to the schema, just not in this module. tests/test_wip_and_stages.py:40 loads schema/state-schema.json, and round 7's MUT-2 (default_stages_for returns []) is GREEN on the compact module and RED on the full suite. So the chain holds by composition -- the schema pins --json, the projection walk pins --compact -- and the blind spot is in one module rather than in the coverage. THE RISK THIS READING ACCEPTS, stated so nobody discovers it later as a surprise: if build() reads the wrong source for a field, --json and --compact carry the SAME wrong number, the standup shows it, both payloads agree and every test passes. That is not criterion 5's subject under this reading, and it is real. It is filed as its own row rather than left implicit. WHY THIS IS NOT THE ROUNDS-EXHAUSTED RULE BEING WAIVED: that rule stops a search with no last element. Four rounds went one layer deeper each and the category is now counted -- ten triples, eleven names, one function. The code has been correct at every round; what failed each time was the evidence that it was correct.
fields.question: What independent source of truth does the --compact projection test have, and if the answer is none, where does criterion 5 stop? TASK-362 has now FAILED FOUR V4 ROUNDS -- the limit is 2 -- and perry-lint reports review-rounds-exhausted on it. FOUR ROUNDS, FOUR DIFFERENT LAYERS OF ONE SHAPE, each found only because the previous fix removed the layer above it: round 4, the RULE was verified by calling the function under test; round 5, the DATA was cardinality one so a projection keeping only the first of anything was green; round 6, the PAIRING resolved each expectation through the very path it was checking, 46 of 53 pairs repointable while green; round 7, the same pairing defect one level down in the subdict children, plus _at itself being shared by the tool and by the test's expectation. ROUND 7 NAMED THE PRINCIPLE PLAINLY AND IT IS A REAL FORK: no test in tests/test_compact_payload.py reads .perry/config.jsonl, okr.jsonl, linkage.jsonl or schema/. --json is the reference on both sides and BOTH COME FROM ONE build(). If build() is wrong, both agree and every test in the module passes. READING 1 -- the criterion's ceiling is that the projection is applied CONSISTENTLY over its whole declaration, an independent source is out of reach for a projection by definition, and the row closes when every declared pair is compared from the key: the ten subdict triples, the eleven arg names, and _at. Bounded, finite, and the fix is already specified by round 7. READING 2 -- criterion 5 says every key carries the same VALUE, so it needs a source outside build(): the store files and schema/ read independently. That is a larger piece of work and would give the module the property it has never had. THE PMO RECOMMENDS READING 1 for this row and READING 2 as a separate row, because the four rounds converged rather than diverged -- each went one level deeper and the category is now enumerated and finite -- and because the rounds-exhausted rule exists to stop a search with no last element, which this no longer is. But the rule is the rule and this is the decision it asks for. WHAT IS ALREADY TRUE regardless of the answer: criterion 13 has held under three independent rounds of attack including five directions round 7 invented, and the code has been correct at every round -- what failed each time was the evidence that it was correct.

fields.question: TASK-439 has FAILed V4 twice and review.md s6 says two FAILs is a decision, not a third round. The READER and the WRITER both key off the phase; only the GATE keys off the file. F-2, WHICH I REPRODUCED WHOLE, IS THE ONE THAT SHOULD DECIDE THIS. With phase/CURRENT cleared -- the state goals/reference/phases.md step 7 PRESCRIBES after score-phase, "until the next plan-phase" -- `add --unlinked` REFUSES ("no key result for the current phase") and `add --kr P004-O9-KR9` is ACCEPTED at exit 0, silently, writing an edge to a KR no record declares; perry-lint says nothing. So in that window the only way past a gate whose own message says "resolve the id through linkage.jsonl rather than guessing it" IS the guess okr-linkage.md forbids. Before this row, all five such states filed the row with a warning. F-1: the refusal promises a standing declaration stays visible in perry-state --section attribution, and that reader passes through linkage_records_for_phase, which keeps a record only while its phase matches phase/CURRENT -- 143 standing declarations on this project, 116 reported, and all 116 go invisible the day 004 opens. Round 1 FAILed the same sentence naming perry-lint; my correction moved the falsehood rather than removing it. THREE READINGS. (A) KEY THE GATE OFF THE PHASE, like the reader and the writer: refuse only when the register declares a KR for the current phase, and fall back to the warning in the gap. fields.question: TASK-236 has now FAILed V4 four times and TWICE since USER-927 picked the last principle, so review.md s6 says the next step is this ask rather than a fifth round. ONE DEFECT, FOUR SPELLINGS, and the round-4 reviewer named the principle better than any of the fixes did: the render joins key results to objectives with `objective_id == obj["id"]`, and NOTHING MAKES THAT AN IDENTITY. Each round excluded one more bad VALUE from that comparison and the next round found another. Round 2: a KR matching no objective was emitted nowhere, so a residual was added -- it lost one row. Round 3: a record with no version slipped past the residual's scoping, so version became required at the validator -- and the blank objective_id it deliberately permitted turned the join into a cross product that invented 75. Round 4: a blank key now matches nothing -- and a DUPLICATE key still matches twice. PMO REPRODUCED ROUND 4'S: perry_md_store mint_objective_ids keys by_title with NO VERSION IN THE KEY, so two objectives sharing a title inside one version block are minted ONE id by Perry's own migration tool; a store holding 3 kr records then renders 6 rows and prints `6 key result(s) under 2 objective(s)` at exit 0, with perry-okr verify rc 0, diff reporting identical true AND every_line_and_cell_came_from_the_store true, and perry-lint clean. Every gate green, the count printed as fact, and the table is not the store. THREE READINGS. (A) MAKE THE IDENTITY A PRECONDITION, CHECKED ONCE: before joining, refuse a version whose objective ids are not unique and non-blank, then look each KR up by id instead of filtering. This ends the sequence -- blank, whitespace, duplicate and anything else are all one rule about the data rather than four rules about values -- and it is the render's own invariant, so it holds however the store was produced. (B) FIX THE MINT: key by_title with the version so two same-titled objectives in one block get different ids. Closes the source this instance came through, but not the category: a hand-written, imported or merged store can still carry duplicates and the render would still cross-product them. It also needs a design answer I do not have -- if title is not the identity inside a block, what is, the heading or the order? (C) BOTH, A now and B as its own row. MY RECOMMENDATION IS A. Four rounds have now patched values one at a time and the fifth would be the same move again; A is the first fix that is about the join rather than about an input to it. B is worth doing and is a different tool, a different invariant and a different design question, so it deserves its own row rather than riding along. ALSO IN FRONT OF YOU, SMALLER, AND NOT PART OF THIS CHOICE: round 3's other finding is still open and I measured that fixing it is a CONTRACT change -- making viewer/parsers.py load_okr_store validate reddens 15 of 35 in test_contract_key_parity, the published-key contract, so perry-goals list and perry-state read a store that perry-goals krs refuses. The proof of adequacy is that on a project where the file still exists, the store-only render is byte-identical to it. TWO, session detection that does not key on BOARD.md existing: work/SKILL.md:108 activates the lane on the file and :292 bootstraps when it is missing, so deleting it would make every new session treat the project as never set up. fields.question: TASK-237 cannot delete BOARD.md as specified, and its own spec is what stops it. The spec requires the row to answer the reading question for a board on its own measurement, and says: if no command is an adequate reading surface for a row's next action, that is a finding and a stop. MEASURED 2026-09-14 ON HEAD. The inherited gate is satisfied -- TASK-236 closed at V4 and its read-surface report is positive, so ADR-010's reopen conditions are not triggered. The row's own gate is not. BOARD.md is 154,151 bytes, 99.4% table, 15 columns; the longest next action in the store is 2,218 bytes. perry-task list prints 4 of 15 columns; perry-explain TASK-391 prints 702 bytes and drops the next action; list --json carries it whole but is a payload. perry-tasks render prints the board byte-identical to BOARD.md -- and with BOARD.md deleted it REFUSES, rc 1, zero bytes, because it fills the task rows IN PLACE over the file on disk. The one adequate surface is fed by the file this row deletes. A SECOND BLOCKER THE SPEC DID NOT LIST: work/SKILL.md:108 activates the lane when a project CONTAINS BOARD.md, and :292 starts bootstrap when it does not, so every new session would treat this project as never set up. THREE READINGS. (A) BUILD THE READ SURFACE FIRST, AS THIS ROW'S FIRST DELIVERABLE: a board render from tasks.jsonl alone -- every row, every column, cells whole, to stdout, no file underneath -- plus session detection that does not key on the file; delete only once both are measured. A real renderer, because section order, header prose and the column layout live only in the file today. No new row. (B) KEEP BOARD.md AS A GENERATED FILE and do not delete it: the board stays a drift-checked render written to disk. Cheapest, and it amends ADR-010, whose title is that BOARD.md stops existing -- a decide-lane change. (C) DELETE ANYWAY, accepting list --json as the reading surface. Not recommended: it is the stop the spec names. MY RECOMMENDATION IS A. ADR-010's direction stands; what is unfinished is DESIGN-013 section 6's order -- prove the render on the thing it replaces before removing the thing.

fields.question: TASK-474 has FAILed V4 twice and both FAILs are one undecided principle: WHO OWNS NEWLINE NORMALISATION for a tier-1 phase document. Round 1: perry-goals split lines two ways internally. Round 2: the splitter was unified but the READER was not — perry-goals reads a body with read_bytes().decode() (byte-faithful, a lone CR is not a line break) while perry-lint reads with read_text() (universal newlines, a lone CR IS one). A 300-line body containing one CR is written at exit 0 and the project's own linter immediately calls it 301 lines over a hard cap of 300. Reproduced by me, not taken on the reviewer's report. Rule 1 says enumerate the category; two FAILs means the category is a fork nobody has taken, so this is the choice rather than a third round. (A) THE WRITER NORMALISES: phase new translates every line break in the supplied body to LF before writing, so the bytes on disk contain only LF and every reader agrees whatever call it uses. Defensible applied consistently: one owner, one place, and the cap count stops depending on who asks. Cost: the writer silently rewrites the author's bytes, which is exactly what Okr.render refuses to do and says so in its docstring — a document that still lints and no longer reads the way its author wrote it. (B) ONE DECLARED READ RULE ACROSS TOOLS: perry-goals and perry-lint are made to read identically, guarded across bin/ rather than inside one function pair. Defensible applied consistently: nothing rewrites anyone's bytes, and the rule becomes checkable for every current and future reader. Cost: it touches bin/perry-lint and any other reader, which is outside TASK-474's declared Files in scope, so it widens this row or becomes its own. WHAT IS ALREADY TRUE: the phase lifecycle writer is merged on main at 8b6078f7; both suites were green; the round-2 review PASSes criteria 1, 2, 6, 7, 8 and 9 and FAILs 3, with 5 flagged. perry-goals already carries the rule for the SPLIT half in two docstrings and a guard added this round. Nothing in schema/state-schema.json declares how a line is counted; bin/perry-lint decides it at :844. I RECOMMEND (A) for the cap path only, not for the document body: count the cap from a normalised copy so the gate agrees with the linter, and keep writing the author's bytes unchanged. That takes neither cost — no rewrite of the user's text, no edit to another tool — and it is the narrowest thing that makes criterion 3 true. Say A, B, my narrowed A, or stop the row.

Round 1: work/SKILL.md sent help-ROW rendering into a procedure whose step 1 runs perry-config show --json and perry-state --section project, on the Explain route, which runs no recovery gate. My round-2 paragraph made it explicit, writing that rows are 'the one thing' the procedure is not applied to. I reproduced the chain before accepting the finding. (A) ROUTE-SCOPED: the pack procedure never runs on Explain, whatever Explain is loading; pack-dependent content is printed MARKED as needing that pack. A blacklist of English hedges cannot be completed. Whichever principle you pick, its guard must assert the rule's shape POSITIVELY rather than forbid known softenings.
